## Biodiversity & Land Use Management score The Biodiversity & Land Use Management score evaluates the company’s ability to manage its exposure to risks on this Key Issue. It is based on the weighted average of the score associated with each relevant indicator, modified by Controversies. This score is derived from indicators that are scored on a 0-10 scale, with 10 corresponding to best practice and 0 corresponding to lack of management. Refer to the Analyzing risk management section of “ESG Ratings Methodology” for additional details. Sources are company disclosures except where otherwise indicated. MSCI S&C uses the following formula to calculate the Biodiversity & Land Use Management score - Excluding Controversies: $$ M G M T _ { i } = \ \sum I n d i c a t o r \_ S c o r e _ { j , i } \ast I n d i c a t o r \_ W e i g h t _ { j , i } $$ Where: $M G M T _ { i }$ is the Management score - Excluding Controversies for company i. $Indicator\_Score_{j,i}$ is the score of indicator j for company i. $I n d i c a t o r \_ W e i g h t _ { j , i }$ is the weight of indicator for company . The following formula is used to calculate the scores for the components $$ C O M P _ { c , i } = \sum _ { j \in c } I n d i c a t o r \_ S c o r e _ { j , i } * I n d i c a t o r \_ W e i g h t \_ S c a l e d _ { j , i } $$ Where: $C O M P _ { c , i }$ is the component score for component $c _ { \prime }$ for company i. $Indicator\_Score_{j,i}$ is the score of indicator j for company i. $Indicator\_Weight\_Scaled_{j,i}$ is the scaled weight of indicator j for company i. $j \in c$ indicates that the summation is over all indicators belonging to component The following formula is used to calculate the weights for the components $$ C O M P \_ W e i g h t _ { c , i } = \sum _ { j \in c } I n d i c a t o r \_ W e i g h t _ { j , i } $$ Where: $C O M P \_ W e i g h t _ { c , i }$ is the component weight for component for company i. $Indicator\_Weight_{j,i}$ is the weight of indicator j for company i. $j \in c$ indicates that the summation is over all indicators belonging to component . The definitions of the data points in each component are given below: ## Biodiversity & Land Use Policy & Disclosure score The Biodiversity & Land Use Policy & Disclosure score evaluates the company’s disclosure of biodiversity and land use policies, including commitments to habitat restoration, minimizing disturbances, engagement with external stakeholders or standard to address the biodiversity impacts of operations. it is expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates strong initiatives. • Involvement with external stakeholder groups to address the biodiversity impacts of its operations Definition: Indicates whether there are external stakeholder groups that work with the company to address the biodiversity impacts of its operations. • Scope of third-party engagement or standard to address the biodiversity impacts of operations Definition: The estimated share of operations with ecosystem protection programs certified or assured by an external stakeholder group. ## • Commitment to minimize disturbances on biodiversity Definition: Indicates whether the company has disclosed an explicit commitment to minimize disturbances on biodiversity, for example following the mitigation hierarchy of “avoid, minimize, restore and offset.” ## • Commitment to reclaim habitat on disturbed land Definition: Indicates whether the company has disclosed an explicit policy to eventually reclaim the habitat of all disturbed land. ## • Scope of biodiversity and land reclamation policy Definition: The scope of operations covered by the company’s disclosed biodiversity and land reclamation policy, where applicable (i.e., all operations including its supply chain, all direct operations, or partial operations). ## Biodiversity & Land Use Programs & Structures score The Biodiversity & Land Programs & Structures score evaluates the company’s ability to manage biodiversity impacts through structured programs and practices, including ecosystem protection initiatives and biodiversity impact assessments for new operations. it is expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates strong initiatives. ## • Extent of programs to protect ecosystems Definition: Assesses the comprehensiveness of the company’s steps to protect ecosystems, for example, whether the company creates ecosystem reserves vs. isolated initiatives to protect single species, and whether such practices apply to all major sites or only selected operations. ## • Conducts biodiversity impact assessments Definition: Indicates whether the company conducts biodiversity impact assessments prior to settling in new areas. ## Biodiversity & Land Use Performance score The Biodiversity & Land Use Performance score evaluates the company's performance on biodiversity & land use metrics (oil spill intensity) relative to its peers. It is expressed as a 0-10 score, with 10 indicating strong performance. ## • Oil spills performance relative to peers Definition: Assesses the company’s performance on oil spills intensity (normalized by sales), and trend in oil spills intensity, relative to its peers. Expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates the highest level of performance. ## ◦ Oil spill intensity industry relative score Definition: Assesses the company’s performance on oil spill intensity metrics (total volume of oil spilled normalized by sales) relative to its industry peers. Expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates strong performance. ## • Three-year average oil spill intensity (sales based) Definition: Measures the company’s three-year average oil spill intensity, calculated as total oil spill volume per unit of sales. ## ◦ Oil spill intensity industry relative trend score Definition: Assesses the company’s performance on the three-year trend in oil spill intensity (year-over-year change in oil spill volume normalized by sales) relative to its industry peers. Expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates strong performance. ## • Three-year average year-over-year oil spill intensity trend (sales based) Definition: Measures the company’s three-year trend in oil spill intensity. ## Controversies A controversy deduction ranging from 0 to 5 points is subtracted from the overall Management score based on the severity, status, and the company’s role in the controversies facing the company on this Key Issue. The result is the Management score. The following categories of controversies are used in the assessment: • Biodiversity & land use controversies. • Oil spills. • Toxic releases to water/land controversies. For more details on how controversies are included in the MSCI ESG Ratings model, refer to Section: Controversies cases, of “ESG Ratings Methodology.” ## Biodiversity & Land Use Exposure score The Biodiversity & Land Use Exposure score evaluates the company’s exposure to risks on this Key Issue. It is based on the Business and Geographic Exposure scores. The Geographic Exposure score functions as a multiplier on the Business Exposure score, with an impact ranging from -50% to +50%. The Business and Geographic Exposure scores are scored on a 0-10 scale, with 10 corresponding to the highest risk and 0 corresponding to the lowest risk. Refer to Section: Analyzing risk exposure, of “ESG Ratings Methodology” for additional details. The following formula is used in the Exposure score calculation: $$ E X P _ { B I O , i } = B U S _ { B I O , i } ( 1 + 0 . 1 \big ( G E O _ { B I O , i } - 5 \big ) ) $$ Where: $E X P _ { B I O , i }$ is the Biodiversity & Land Use Exposure score of company i. $B U S _ { B I O , i }$ is the Business Exposure score of company i. $G E O _ { B I O , i }$ is the Geographic Exposure score of company i. Exhibit 2: Exposure score components Biodiversity & Land Use Exposure Score Business Exposure Score Geographic Exposure Score Business Segment Exposure Scores Geographic Segment Exposure Scores Biodiversity Business Impacts, Controversies Forest Area Loss, Threatened Species ## Business Exposure score The Business Exposure score is a weighted average of the Segment Exposure scores of a company’s business segments. MSCI S&C weights scores by the proportion of a company’s total assets in each business segment,2 using the following formula to calculate the Business Exposure score: $$ B U S _ { B I O , i } = \sum _ { j = 1 } ^ { n _ { i } } w _ { A s s e t , i , j } B S E _ { B I O , j } $$ Where: $B S E _ { B I O , j }$ is the Business Segment Exposure score for business segment j. $w _ { A s s e t , i , j }$ is the weight of business segment j for company i based on the contribution to total company assets. $n _ { i }$ is the number of business segments of company i. ## Business Segment Exposure scores The Business Segment Exposure score of a business segment is based on a mapping of the business segment as disclosed by the company to a corresponding business activity. MSCI S&C uses the Standard Industrial Classification (SIC) system along with industry-specific adjustments to define business activities. The score associated with a business activity is used to calculate a Business Segment Exposure score. Each business activity score is determined by a simple average of the Biodiversity Business Impacts score and the Controversies score of the business activity. $$ B S E _ { B I O , j } = \frac { B B I S _ { j } + C S _ { j } } { 2 } $$ Where: $B B I S _ { j }$ is the Biodiversity Business Impacts score for business activity j. $C S _ { j }$ is the Controversies score for business activity j. The Biodiversity Business Impacts score of a business activity is assessed by examining the business impacts that are present for that activity. Nine business impacts arising from biodiversity and ecosystem changes are considered such as disruption of operations, restricted access to land and resources and litigation. For each business activity, each impact is presented as a 0 or 1 value, with 1 indicating that the impact is present. The number of impacts that apply to each activity is counted and scaled to a factor of 10 to calculate the Biodiversity Business Impacts score. The Controversies score of a business activity is determined by the percentage of companies involved in a biodiversity controversy assessed as Moderate to Very Severe among all the companies with the same primary business activity.3 Refer to Section: Controversies cases, of “ESG Ratings Methodology” for details on how the severity of controversy cases is assessed. ## Geographic Exposure score The Geographic Exposure score is a weighted average of the Geographic Segment Exposure scores of the countries, markets and regions in which a company operates. MSCI S&C weighs scores by the proportion of a company’s total assets in each geographic segment through the following equation: $$ G E O _ { B I O , i } = \sum _ { r = 1 } ^ { n _ { i } } w _ { A s s e t , i , r } G S E _ { B I O , r } $$ Where: $G S E _ { B I O , r }$ is the Geographic Segment Exposure score of region . $w _ { A s s e t , i , r }$ is the weight of total assets in region r for company i based on the contribution to total company assets. $n _ { i }$ is the number of geographic segments for company i. For geographic segments disclosed as regions (example: Asia Pacific), a nominal GDP-weighted country or market aggregation is used to calculate region-level scores, using the following equation: $$ G S E _ { B I O , r } = \sum _ { c = 1 } ^ { n _ { r } } w _ { G D P , r , c } G S E _ { B I O , c } $$ Where: $G S E _ { B I O , c }$ is the Geographic Segment Exposure score of country or market . $w _ { G D P , r , c }$ is the specific weight of country or market within region . ## Geographic Segment Exposure scores The Geographic Segment Exposure score is determined by a simple average of (1) average annual forest area loss score, and (2) the number of threatened species score in the country or market: $$ G S E _ { B I O , c } = { \frac { A F L _ { c } + N T S _ { c } } { 2 } } $$ Where: $A F L _ { c }$ is the average annual forest area loss score in country or market . It is calculated from the 5-year average annual forest area loss (1,000 Ha) per country or market. $N T S _ { c }$ is the number of threatened species score in country or market . ## Data sources The following sources are used to determine the Biodiversity & Land Use Exposure score: World Resources Institute, “Global Forest Watch;” World Resources Institute; UNDP Human Development Reports; Refinitiv; MSCI S&C; company disclosures. ## Contact us ## About MSCI Inc. blocks.content: This document provides essential information on the components of the Raw Material Sourcing Key Issue to enable users of ESG Ratings to understand how MSCI Sustainability & Climate’s (MSCI S&C’s),1 outputs are determined. Raw Material Sourcing is a Key Issue in the Environmental Pillar of the MSCI ESG Ratings model. Companies are evaluated on the environmental impacts of the raw materials used in their products and their efforts around supply-chain traceability and certification.
For additional details on the MSCI ESG Ratings Model, refer to the Data, ratings and scores section of ”ESG Ratings Methodology.”

The Key Issue score is based on the Exposure score and the Management score using the formula below. The Exposure score and the Management score are combined such that a higher level of exposure requires a higher level of demonstrated management capability in order to achieve the same overall Key Issue score.

sections.title_en: Raw Material Sourcing Beef & Dairy Policy score

blocks.content: The Raw Material Sourcing Beef & Dairy Policy score evaluates the company’s initiatives to manage the environmental and social impacts of beef and dairy sourcing through policies, certification, traceability and supplier programs. Highest initiatives reflect clear commitments, measurable targets, stringent certification, and full traceability across the supply chain. It is expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates strong initiatives.Commitments towards responsible beef and/or dairy sourcing.

Definition: Indicates whether the company has an explicit policy to sustainably source beef and/or dairy (e.g., zero-deforestation beef policy) or whether it belongs to an industry group with such a policy (e.g., the Global Roundtable on Responsible Beef).
• Percentage of beef and/or dairy third-party certified to an environmental sustainability standard.
Definition: The estimated share of beef and/or dairy externally certified to sustainable standards (e.g., organic certification).

sections.title_en: • Extent of beef and/or dairy certification against the most stringent sustainable criteria.

blocks.content: Definition: The estimated share of the company’s supply of beef and/or dairy externally certified to the most stringent sustainable standards (e.g., Rainforest Alliance).

sections.title_en: • Extent of beef and/or dairy traceability to place of origin.

blocks.content: Definition: The estimated level of traceability of beef and/or dairy up to the plantation/farm level. Best practice is for all products to be traceable.

sections.title_en: • Extent of supply chain initiatives to address impacts of beef and/or dairy production.

blocks.content: Definition: The extent of the company’s initiatives to develop sustainable practices within its beef and/or dairy supply chain, e.g., sustainable land management program, methane reduction program, implementation of specific sustainable requirements for suppliers and verification of compliance.

sections.title_en: • Future targets for beef and/or dairy sourcing.

blocks.content: Definition: The extent to which the company has clear, measurable targets for certifying or tracing its sources of beef and/or dairy.

sections.title_en: Raw Material Sourcing Cotton Policy score

blocks.content: The Raw Material Sourcing Cotton Policy score evaluates the company’s initiatives to manage the environmental and social impacts of Cotton sourcing through policies, certification, traceability and supplier programs. Highest initiatives reflect clear commitments, measurable targets, stringent certification, and full traceability across the supply chain. It is expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates strong initiatives.Commitments towards responsible cotton sourcing.

Definition: Indicates whether the company has an explicit policy to sustainably source cotton or whether it belongs to an industry group with such a policy (e.g., Textile Exchange or Better Cotton Initiative).

sections.title_en: • Percentage of cotton third-party certified to an environmental standard.

blocks.content: Definition: The estimated share of cotton externally certified to sustainable standards (e.g., Better Cotton Initiative).

sections.title_en: • Extent of cotton traceability to place of origin.

blocks.content: Definition: The estimated level of traceability of cotton up to the plantation/farm level. Best practice is for all products to be traceable.

sections.title_en: • Extent of supply chain initiatives to address impacts of cotton production.

blocks.content: Definition: The extent of the company’s initiatives to develop sustainable practices within its cotton supply chain, e.g., water and pesticide reduction programs, technical assistance to obtain sustainable certification.

sections.title_en: • Future targets for cotton sourcing.

blocks.content: Definition: The extent to which the company has clear, measurable targets for certifying or tracing its sources of cotton.

sections.title_en: Raw Material Sourcing Leather Policy score

blocks.content: The Raw Material Sourcing Leather Policy score evaluates the company’s initiatives to manage the environmental and social impacts of leather sourcing through policies, certification, traceability, and supplier programs. Highest initiatives reflect clear commitments, measurable targets, stringent certification and full traceability across the supply chain. It is expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates strong initiatives.

sections.title_en: • Commitments towards responsible leather sourcing.

blocks.content: Definition: Indicates whether the company has an explicit policy to sustainably source leather (e.g., addressing deforestation) or whether it belongs to an industry group with such a policy (e.g., Leather Working Group).

sections.title_en: • Percentage of leather third-party certified to an environmental sustainability standard.

blocks.content: Definition: The estimated share of leather externally certified to sustainable standards (e.g., Leather Working Group).

sections.title_en: • Extent of leather certification against the most stringent sustainable criteria.

blocks.content: Definition: The estimated share of the company’s supply of leather externally certified to the most stringent sustainable standards (e.g., Recycled).

sections.title_en: • Extent of leather traceability to place of origin.

blocks.content: Definition: The estimated level of traceability of leather up to the plantation/farm level. Best practice is for all products to be traceable.

sections.title_en: • Extent of supply chain initiatives to address impacts of leather production.

blocks.content: Definition: The extent of the company’s initiatives to develop sustainable practices within its leather supply chain, e.g., technical assistance to obtain sustainable certification, reduction of chemical use in the dyeing and tanning process.

sections.title_en: • Future targets for leather sourcing.

blocks.content: Definition: The extent to which the company has clear, measurable targets for certifying or tracing its sources of leather.

blocks.content: Definition: Indicates whether the company has an explicit policy to sustainably source palm oil (e.g., no deforestation, no peat, no exploitation policy) or whether it belongs to an industry group with such a policy (e.g., the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil).

sections.title_en: • Percentage of palm oil third-party certified to an environmental sustainability standard.

blocks.content: Definition: The estimated share of palm oil externally certified to sustainable standards (e.g., Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil).

sections.title_en: • Extent of palm oil certification against the most stringent sustainable criteria.

blocks.content: Definition: The estimated share of the company’s supply of palm oil externally certified to the most stringent sustainable standards (e.g., Segregated or Identity Preserved Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil).

sections.title_en: • Extent of palm oil traceability to place of origin.

blocks.content: Definition: The estimated level of traceability of palm oil up to the plantation/farm level. Best practice is for all products to be traceable.

sections.title_en: • Extent of supply chain initiatives to address impacts of palm oil production.

blocks.content: Definition: The extent of the company’s initiatives to develop sustainable practices within its palm oil supply chain, e.g., technical assistance to obtain sustainable certification, implementation of specific sustainable requirements for suppliers and verification of compliance.

sections.title_en: • Future targets for palm oil sourcing.

blocks.content: Definition: The extent to which the company has clear, measurable targets for certifying or tracing its sources of palm oil.

sections.title_en: Raw Material Sourcing Seafood Policy score

blocks.content: The Raw Material Sourcing Seafood Policy score evaluates the company’s initiatives to manage the environmental and social impacts of seafood sourcing through policies, certification, traceability and supplier programs. It is expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates strong initiatives.

sections.title_en: • Commitments towards responsible seafood sourcing.

blocks.content: Definition: Indicates whether the company has an explicit policy to sustainably source seafood (e.g., banning the sale of endangered species, specifying acceptable fishing methods) or whether it belongs to an industry group with such a policy (e.g., Marine Stewardship Council).

sections.title_en: • Percentage of seafood third-party certified to an environmental sustainability standard.

blocks.content: Definition: The estimated share of seafood externally certified to sustainable standards (e.g., Global Aquaculture Alliance’s Best Aquaculture Practices).

sections.title_en: • Extent of seafood certification against the most stringent sustainable criteria.

blocks.content: Definition: The estimated share of the company’s supply of seafood externally certified to the most stringent sustainable standards (e.g., Marine Stewardship Council, Aquaculture Stewardship Council).

sections.title_en: • Extent of seafood traceability to place of origin.

blocks.content: Definition: The estimated level of traceability of seafood up to the fishing location/farm level. Best practice is for all products to be traceable.

sections.title_en: • Extent of supply chain initiatives to address impacts of seafood production.

blocks.content: Definition: The extent of the company’s initiatives to develop sustainable practices within its seafood supply chain, e.g., technical assistance to obtain sustainable certification, involvement in Fisheries Improvement Projects.

sections.title_en: • Future targets for seafood sourcing.

blocks.content: Definition: The extent to which the company has clear, measurable targets for certifying or tracing its sources of seafood.

sections.title_en: Raw Material Sourcing Timber Policy score

blocks.content: The Raw Material Sourcing Timber Policy score evaluates the company’s initiatives to manage the environmental and social impacts of timber sourcing through policies, certification, traceability, and supplier programs. Highest initiatives reflect clear commitments, measurable targets, stringent certification and full traceability across the supply chain. It is expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates strong initiatives.

sections.title_en: • Commitments towards responsible timber and/or paper sourcing.

blocks.content: Definition: Indicates whether the company has an explicit policy to sustainably source timber or whether it belongs to an industry group with such a policy (e.g., Forest Stewardship Council).
• Percentage of timber or paper third-party certified to an environmental sustainability standard.
Definition: The estimated share of timber or paper externally certified to sustainable standards (e.g., Programme for the Endorsement of Forest Certification).

sections.title_en: • Extent of timber certification against the most stringent sustainable criteria.

blocks.content: Definition: The estimated share of the company’s supply of timber externally certified to the most stringent sustainable standards (e.g., Forest Stewardship Council).

sections.title_en: • Extent of timber and/or paper traceability to place of origin.

blocks.content:
Definition: The estimated level of traceability of timber and/or paper up to the plantation or forest level. 
Best practice is for all products to be traceable.

sections.title_en: • Extent of supply chain initiatives to address impacts of timber and/or paper production.

blocks.content: Definition: The extent of the company’s initiatives to develop sustainable practices within its timber and/or paper supply chain, e.g., technical assistance to obtain sustainable certification, implementation of specific sustainable requirements for suppliers and verification of compliance.

sections.title_en: • Future targets for timber and/or paper sourcing.

blocks.content: Definition: The extent to which the company has clear, measurable targets for certifying or tracing its sources of timber and/or paper.
Sources: company disclosures; Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil; other stakeholder working groups, for example, Rainforest Alliance, Better Cotton, Textile Exchange, Leather Working Group.

It is expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates strong initiatives. ## • Commitments towards responsible leather sourcing. Definition: Indicates whether the company has an explicit policy to sustainably source leather (e.g., addressing deforestation) or whether it belongs to an industry group with such a policy (e.g., Leather Working Group). ## • Percentage of leather third-party certified to an environmental sustainability standard. Definition: The estimated share of leather externally certified to sustainable standards (e.g., Leather Working Group). ## • Extent of leather certification against the most stringent sustainable criteria. Definition: The estimated share of the company’s supply of leather externally certified to the most stringent sustainable standards (e.g., Recycled). ## • Extent of leather traceability to place of origin. Definition: The estimated level of traceability of leather up to the plantation/farm level. Best practice is for all products to be traceable. ## • Extent of supply chain initiatives to address impacts of leather production. Definition: The extent of the company’s initiatives to develop sustainable practices within its leather supply chain, e.g., technical assistance to obtain sustainable certification, reduction of chemical use in the dyeing and tanning process. ## • Future targets for leather sourcing. Definition: The extent to which the company has clear, measurable targets for certifying or tracing its sources of leather. ## Raw Material Sourcing Palm Oil Policy score The Raw Material Sourcing Palm Oil Policy score evaluates the company’s initiatives to manage the environmental and social impacts of palm oil sourcing through policies, certification, traceability and supplier programs. Highest initiatives reflect clear commitments, measurable targets, stringent certification, and full traceability across the supply chain. It is expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates strong initiatives. ## • Commitments towards responsible palm oil sourcing. Definition: Indicates whether the company has an explicit policy to sustainably source palm oil (e.g., no deforestation, no peat, no exploitation policy) or whether it belongs to an industry group with such a policy (e.g., the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil). ## • Percentage of palm oil third-party certified to an environmental sustainability standard. Definition: The estimated share of palm oil externally certified to sustainable standards (e.g., Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil). ## • Extent of palm oil certification against the most stringent sustainable criteria. Definition: The estimated share of the company’s supply of palm oil externally certified to the most stringent sustainable standards (e.g., Segregated or Identity Preserved Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil). ## • Extent of palm oil traceability to place of origin. Definition: The estimated level of traceability of palm oil up to the plantation/farm level. Best practice is for all products to be traceable. ## • Extent of supply chain initiatives to address impacts of palm oil production. Definition: The extent of the company’s initiatives to develop sustainable practices within its palm oil supply chain, e.g., technical assistance to obtain sustainable certification, implementation of specific sustainable requirements for suppliers and verification of compliance. ## • Future targets for palm oil sourcing. Definition: The extent to which the company has clear, measurable targets for certifying or tracing its sources of palm oil. ## Raw Material Sourcing Seafood Policy score The Raw Material Sourcing Seafood Policy score evaluates the company’s initiatives to manage the environmental and social impacts of seafood sourcing through policies, certification, traceability and supplier programs. Highest initiatives reflect clear commitments, measurable targets, stringent certification, and full traceability across the supply chain. It is expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates strong initiatives. ## • Commitments towards responsible seafood sourcing. Definition: Indicates whether the company has an explicit policy to sustainably source seafood (e.g., banning the sale of endangered species, specifying acceptable fishing methods) or whether it belongs to an industry group with such a policy (e.g., Marine Stewardship Council). ## • Percentage of seafood third-party certified to an environmental sustainability standard. Definition: The estimated share of seafood externally certified to sustainable standards (e.g., Global Aquaculture Alliance’s Best Aquaculture Practices). ## • Extent of seafood certification against the most stringent sustainable criteria. Definition: The estimated share of the company’s supply of seafood externally certified to the most stringent sustainable standards (e.g., Marine Stewardship Council, Aquaculture Stewardship Council). ## • Extent of seafood traceability to place of origin. Definition: The estimated level of traceability of seafood up to the fishing location/farm level. Best practice is for all products to be traceable. ## • Extent of supply chain initiatives to address impacts of seafood production. Definition: The extent of the company’s initiatives to develop sustainable practices within its seafood supply chain, e.g., technical assistance to obtain sustainable certification, involvement in Fisheries Improvement Projects. ## • Future targets for seafood sourcing. Definition: The extent to which the company has clear, measurable targets for certifying or tracing its sources of seafood. ## Raw Material Sourcing Timber Policy score The Raw Material Sourcing Timber Policy score evaluates the company’s initiatives to manage the environmental and social impacts of timber sourcing through policies, certification, traceability, and supplier programs. Highest initiatives reflect clear commitments, measurable targets, stringent certification and full traceability across the supply chain. It is expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates strong initiatives. ## • Commitments towards responsible timber and/or paper sourcing. Definition: Indicates whether the company has an explicit policy to sustainably source timber or whether it belongs to an industry group with such a policy (e.g., Forest Stewardship Council). • Percentage of timber or paper third-party certified to an environmental sustainability standard. Definition: The estimated share of timber or paper externally certified to sustainable standards (e.g., Programme for the Endorsement of Forest Certification). ## • Extent of timber certification against the most stringent sustainable criteria. Definition: The estimated share of the company’s supply of timber externally certified to the most stringent sustainable standards (e.g., Forest Stewardship Council). ## • Extent of timber and/or paper traceability to place of origin. Definition: The estimated level of traceability of timber and/or paper up to the plantation or forest level. Best practice is for all products to be traceable. ## • Extent of supply chain initiatives to address impacts of timber and/or paper production. Definition: The extent of the company’s initiatives to develop sustainable practices within its timber and/or paper supply chain, e.g., technical assistance to obtain sustainable certification, implementation of specific sustainable requirements for suppliers and verification of compliance. ## • Future targets for timber and/or paper sourcing. Definition: The extent to which the company has clear, measurable targets for certifying or tracing its sources of timber and/or paper. Sources: company disclosures; Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil; other stakeholder working groups, for example, Rainforest Alliance, Better Cotton, Textile Exchange, Leather Working Group. ## Controversies A controversy deduction ranging from 0 to 5 points is subtracted from the overall Management score based on the severity, status, and the company’s role in the controversies facing the company on this Key Issue. The following categories of controversies are used in the assessment: • Environmental issues in the supply chain controversies. For more details on how controversies are included in the MSCI ESG Ratings model, refer to the Controversies cases section of ”ESG Ratings Methodology.” ## Raw Material Sourcing Exposure score The Raw Material Sourcing Exposure score evaluates the company’s exposure to risks on this Key Issue. It is based on the Company-Specific Exposure Score only. The Company-Specific Exposure Score is scored on a 0-10 scale, with 10 corresponding to the highest risk and 0 corresponding to the lowest risk. Refer to the Analyzing risk exposure section of “ESG Ratings Methodology” for additional details. The following formula is used in the Exposure score calculation: $$ E X P _ { R M S , i } = C O M _ { R M S , i } $$ Where: $E X P _ { R M S , i }$ is the Raw Material Sourcing Exposure score of company i. $C O M _ { R M S , i }$ is the Company-Specific Exposure score of company i. Exhibit 2: Exposure score components 敞口组成图所在官方原件页：原材料采购，第14页（图页见本议题结构化正文；官网来源：https://www.msci.com/downloads/documents/access/sustainability-and-climate-resources-and-disclosures/msci-sustainability-and-climate-methodologies/esg-ratings/esg-key-issue-methodologies/environmental-pillar/raw-materials-sourcing-key-issue.pdf） ## Company-Specific Exposure score The Company-Specific Exposure score is a simple average of the Dependency score and the Footprint score, sourced by company i. $$ C O M _ { R M S , i } = \frac { D S _ { R M S , i } + F S _ { R M S , i } } { 2 } $$ Where: $D S _ { R M S , i }$ is the Dependency score of company i. $F S _ { R M S , i }$ is the Footprint score of company i. The Footprint score is calculated as: $$ F S _ { R M S , i } = { \it S c a l e } _ { 0 - 1 0 } \left\{ E S R _ { R M S , i } \ \times \ 3 \ y r \ a v g e r a g e \ s a l e s _ { \ R M S , i } \right\} $$ Where: $E S R _ { R M S , i }$ is the Estimated Sales Reliant on all raw materials of concern of company i. 3-year sales average of company i. The Footprint score assesses the company’s exposure to environmental risks from the use of raw material of concern, calculated using the percentage of sales reliant on all raw materials of concern, multiplied by the company’s three-year sales average, adjusted for private label share where applicable. The Dependency score is derived as: $$ { \cal D } S _ { R M S , i } = { \cal S } c a l e _ { 0 - 1 0 } \left\{ { \cal E } S R _ { R M S , i } \right\} $$ Where: $E S R _ { R M S , i }$ is the Estimated Sales Reliant on all raw materials of concern of company i. The Dependency score assesses the company’s dependence on materials of concern based on the percentage of sales reliant on all raw materials of concern. ## Data sources The following sources are used to determine the Raw Material Sourcing Exposure score: Refinitiv, MSCI S&C, company disclosures. ## Contact us ## About MSCI Inc. sections.title_en: Introduction

blocks.content: This document provides essential information on the components of the Toxic Emissions & Waste Key Issue to enable users of ESG Ratings to understand how MSCI Sustainability & Climate’s (MSCI S&C’s)1 outputs are determined. Toxic Emissions & Waste is a Key Issue in the Environmental Pillar of the MSCI ESG Ratings model. Companies are evaluated on the potential environmental contamination and toxic or carcinogenic emissions arising from their operations and the strength of their environmental management systems.
For additional details on the MSCI ESG Ratings Model, refer to the Data, ratings and scores section of “ESG Ratings Methodology.”

sections.title_en: Toxic Emissions & Waste Key Issue score

blocks.content: The Toxic Emissions & Waste Key Issue score evaluates the company’s level of exposure to, and management of, risks on this Key Issue. The Key Issue score is based on the Exposure score and the Management score using the formula below. The Exposure score and the Management score are combined such that a higher level of exposure requires a higher level of demonstrated management capability in order to achieve the same overall Key Issue score.

$$
K I _ { i } = 7 - ( \operatorname* { m a x } { ( E X P _ { i } , 2 ) } - M G M T _ { i } )
$$
Where:
$K I _ { i }$ is the Key Issue score for company i.
$E X P _ { i }$ is the Exposure score for company i.
$M G M T _ { i }$ is the Management score for company i.

sections.title_en: Toxic Emissions & Waste Governance and Strategy score

blocks.content: The Toxic Emissions & Waste Governance and Strategy score evaluates the company’s initiatives to govern and manage toxic emissions and waste through policies, environmental management systems, certifications, audits, and supply chain programs. Highest initiatives reflect comprehensive policies, certified systems, and proactive oversight across operations and suppliers. It is expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates strong initiatives.

sections.title_en: • Scope and frequency of environmental impact audits

blocks.content: Definition: Assesses whether the company conducts regular audits to assess and manage environmental risks and impacts. Expressed as a 0-10 score, with 10 indicating strong initiatives.

sections.title_en: o Evidence of environmental impact audits

blocks.content: Definition: Indicates whether there is evidence that the company conducts internal and/or external environmental audits of its relevant operations. This could include, for example, an EMS certified to ISO 14001 or a similar framework, which requires regular audits.

sections.title_en: ◦ Evidence of audits across all locations of operations

blocks.content: Definition: Indicates whether there is evidence of environmental audits across all locations of operations.

sections.title_en: ◦ Evidence of annual environmental impact audits

blocks.content: Definition: Indicates whether there is evidence that the company carries out annual environmental impact audits.

sections.title_en: • Existence of environmental management system

blocks.content: Definition: Indicates whether there is evidence that the company has an Environmental Management System (EMS) in place across all or selected relevant operations. This could include, for example, an EMS certified to ISO 14001, registration under EMAS, or a similar framework.

sections.title_en: • Extent of programs to reduce toxic emissions of supply chain

blocks.content: Definition: Indicates the extent to which the company has established programs to reduce toxic emissions within its supply chain. Best practice is for suppliers’ environmental management to be subject to screening and audits.

sections.title_en: • Scope of policies to address environmental impacts

blocks.content: Definition: Indicates whether the company has formal policies in place to address environmental impacts such as air emissions, water discharges, and waste.

sections.title_en: • Certified environmental system score

blocks.content: Definition: Assesses the extent of the company's sites with an environmental management system certified to ISO 14001 or similar. Expressed as a 0-10 score, with 10 indicating the highest degree of certification.

sections.title_en: ◦ Percentage of operations with an environmental management system certified to ISO 14001 or HAZWOPER

blocks.content: Definition: The percentage of sites with hazardous waste guidance that follow ISO 14001 or HAZWOPER certification for waste management.

sections.title_en: Toxic Emissions & Waste Targets score

blocks.content: The Toxic Emissions & Waste Targets score evaluates the company’s initiatives to set and achieve targets for reducing toxic emissions and waste. Highest initiatives reflect comprehensive, quantitative reduction targets with demonstrated progress toward achievement. It is expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates strong initiatives.

sections.title_en: • Toxic emissions & waste target comprehensiveness

blocks.content: Definition: Assesses the extent to which a company has established toxic waste reduction targets that have a measurable reduction scope and are complete in coverage. Expressed as a 0-10 score, with 10 indicating a quantitative target that covers all segments.

sections.title_en: ◦ Evidence of ongoing Toxic Emissions & Waste target

blocks.content: Definition: Indicates whether the company has an ongoing toxic emissions and/or waste reduction target.

sections.title_en: ◦ Scope of ongoing Toxic Emissions & Waste target

blocks.content: Definition: Assess the scope of coverage of the ongoing toxic emissions and/or waste target. Expressed as a 0-10 score, where 10 indicates that the target covers all relevant segments of the company's operations.

sections.title_en: • Toxic emissions & waste target progress

blocks.content: Definition: Assesses the company’s to-date progress on active toxic emissions & waste targets, as well as its historical track record in meeting previously stated targets. Expressed as a 0-10 score, with 10 indicating achievement of stated target.

sections.title_en: ◦ Status of ongoing Toxic Emissions & Waste target

blocks.content: Definition: Measures the current implementation status of the company’s ongoing target on toxic emissions and/or waste management, by assessing the current progress against the target.

sections.title_en: ◦ Status of historical Toxic Emissions & Waste target

blocks.content: Definition: Measures the achievement or completion status of the company’s historical target on toxic emissions and/or waste management, by assessing whether the stated target was achieved or not.

sections.title_en: Toxic Emissions & Waste Performance score

blocks.content: The Toxic Emissions & Waste Performance score evaluates the company's performance on toxic emissions and waste metrics (including NOx emissions, SOx emissions, particulate matter emissions, hazardous and non-hazardous waste, and other relevant pollutants), relative to its peers. It is expressed as a 0-10 score, where 10 indicates strong performance.

sections.title_en: • NOx emissions performance relative to peers

blocks.content: Definition: Assesses the company's performance on nitrogen oxides (NOx) emissions intensity (normalized by sales or by units of production), and trend in NOx emissions intensity, relative to its peers. Expressed as a 0-10 score, where 10 indicates strong performance.

sections.title_en: ◦ NOx emissions intensity industry relative score

blocks.content: Definition: Assesses the company’s performance on nitrogen oxide (NOx) emissions intensity (emissions per unit of sales or production), relative to its peers. Expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates strong performance.

sections.title_en: • Three-year average NOx emissions intensity (sales based)

blocks.content: Definition: Measures the company’s three-year average NOx emissions (per unit of sales).

sections.title_en: • Three-year average NOx emissions intensity (production based)

blocks.content: Definition: Measures the company’s three-year average NOx emissions (per megawatt-hour generated).

sections.title_en: ◦ NOx emissions intensity industry relative trend score

blocks.content: Definition: Assesses the company’s performance on the three-year average of year-over-year NOx emissions (per unit of sales or production) trend, relative to its peers. Expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates strong performance.

sections.title_en: • Three-year average NOx emissions intensity trend (sales based)

blocks.content: Definition: Measures the company’s three-year average of year-over-year NOx emissions (per unit of sales) trend.

sections.title_en: • Three-year average NOx emissions intensity trend (production based)

blocks.content: Definition: Measures the company’s three-year average of year-over-year NOx emissions (per megawatt-hour generated) trend.

sections.title_en: • Three-year average SOx emissions intensity (production based)

blocks.content: Definition: Measures the company’s three-year average SOx emissions (per megawatt-hour generated).

sections.title_en: ◦ SOx emissions intensity industry relative trend score

blocks.content: Definition: Assesses the company’s performance on the three-year average of yearover-year SOx emissions (per unit of sales or production) trend, relative to its peers. Expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates strong performance.

sections.title_en: • Three-year average SOx emissions intensity trend (sales based)

blocks.content: Definition: Measures the company’s three-year average of year-over-year SOx emissions (per unit of sales) trend.

sections.title_en: • Three-year average SOx emissions intensity trend (production based)

blocks.content: Definition: Measures the company’s three-year average of year-over-year SOx emissions (per megawatt-hour generated) trend.

sections.title_en: • VOC emissions performance relative to peers

blocks.content: Definition: Assesses the company's performance on volatile organic compounds (VOC) emissions intensity (normalized by sales), and trend in VOC emissions intensity, relative to its peers. Expressed as a 0-10 score, where 10 indicates strong performance.

sections.title_en: ◦ VOC emissions intensity industry relative score

blocks.content: Definition: Assesses the company’s performance on volatile organic compounds (VOC) emissions intensity (emissions per unit of sales), relative to its peers. Expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates strong performance.

sections.title_en: • Three-year average VOC emissions intensity (sales based)

blocks.content: Definition: Measures the company’s three-year average VOC emissions per unit of sales.

sections.title_en: ◦ VOC emissions intensity (sales based) industry relative trend score

blocks.content: Definition: Assesses the company’s performance on the three-year average of yearover-year VOC emissions (per unit of sales) trend, relative to its peers. Expressed as a 0– 10 score, where 10 indicates strong performance.

sections.title_en: • Three-year average VOC emissions intensity trend (sales based)

blocks.content: Definition: Measures the company’s three-year average of year-over-year VOC emissions (per unit of sales) trend.

sections.title_en: • Particulate matter emissions performance relative to peers

blocks.content: Definition: Assesses the company's performance on particulate matter (PM) emissions intensity (normalized by sales), and trend in PM emissions intensity), relative to its peers. Expressed as a 0-10 score, where 10 indicates strong performance.

sections.title_en: ◦ Particulate matter emissions intensity industry relative score

blocks.content: Definition: Assesses the company’s performance on particulate matter (PM) emissions intensity (emissions per unit of sales) relative to its peers. Expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates strong performance.

sections.title_en: • Three-year average particulate matter emissions intensity (sales based)

blocks.content: Definition: Measures the company’s three-year average particulate matter emissions (per unit of sales).

sections.title_en: ◦ Particulate matter emissions intensity industry relative trend score

blocks.content: Definition: Assesses the company’s performance on the three-year average of yearover-year particulate matter emissions intensity (per unit of sales) trend, relative to its industry peers. Expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates strong performance.

sections.title_en: • Three-year average particulate matter emissions intensity trend (sales based)

blocks.content: Definition: Measures the company’s three-year average of year-over-year particulate matter emissions intensity(per unit of sales) trend.

sections.title_en: • Hazardous waste performance relative to peers

blocks.content: Definition: Assesses the company's performance on hazardous waste intensity (normalized by sales), and trend in hazardous waste intensity, relative to its peers. Expressed as a 0-10 score, where 10 indicates strong performance.

sections.title_en: ◦ Hazardous waste intensity industry relative score

blocks.content: Definition: Assesses the company’s performance on hazardous waste generated normalized by sales, relative to its industry peers. Expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates strong performance.

sections.title_en: • Three-year average hazardous waste intensity (sales based)

blocks.content: Definition: Measures the company’s three-year average hazardous waste generated per unit of sales.

sections.title_en: ◦ Hazardous waste intensity industry relative trend score

blocks.content: Definition: Assesses the company’s performance on the three-year average of yearover-year hazardous waste generated (per unit of sales) trend, relative to its industry peers. Expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates strong performance.

sections.title_en: • Three-year average hazardous waste intensity trend (sales based)

blocks.content: Definition: Measures the company’s three-year average of year-over-year hazardous waste generated (per unit of sales) trend.

sections.title_en: • Non-hazardous waste performance relative to peers

blocks.content: Definition: Assesses the company's performance on non-hazardous waste intensity (normalized by sales), and trend in non-hazardous waste intensity, relative to its peers. Expressed as a 0-10 score, where 10 indicates strong performance.

sections.title_en: ◦ Non-hazardous waste intensity industry relative score

blocks.content: Definition: Assesses the company’s performance on non-hazardous waste generated (normalized by sales), relative to its industry peers. Expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates strong performance.

sections.title_en: • Three-year average non-hazardous waste intensity (sales based)

blocks.content: Definition: Measures the company’s three-year average non-hazardous waste generated (per unit of sales).

sections.title_en: ◦ Non-hazardous waste intensity industry relative trend score

blocks.content: Definition: Assesses the company’s performance on the three-year average of yearover-year non-hazardous generated (per unit of sales) trend, relative to its industry peers. Expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates strong performance.
• Three-year average non-hazardous waste intensity trend (sales based)
Definition: Measures the company’s three-year average of year-over-year nonhazardous waste generated (per unit of sales) trend.
Source: Environmental Protection Agency’s (EPA’s) Resource Conservation and Recovery Act Biennial Reporting.

sections.title_en: Controversies

blocks.content: A controversy deduction ranging from 0 to 5 points is subtracted from the overall Management score based on the severity, status, and the company’s role in the controversies facing the company on this Key Issue. The following categories of controversies are used in the assessment:
• Toxic emissions and spills controversies.
For more details on how controversies are included in the MSCI ESG Ratings model, refer to the Controversies cases section of “ESG Ratings Methodology.”

sections.title_en: Toxic Emissions & Waste Exposure score

The Business Exposure score is scored on a 0-10 scale, with 10 corresponding to the highest risk and 0 corresponding to the lowest risk. sections.title_en: Business Exposure score

blocks.content: The Business Exposure score is a weighted average of the Toxic Emissions & Waste Business Segment Exposure scores of a company’s business segments. scores are weighted by the proportion of a company’s total assets in each business segment,2 using the following formula to calculate the Business Exposure score:
Where:
$B S E _ { T E W , j }$ is the Toxic Emissions & Waste Business Segment Exposure score for business segment j.
$w _ { A s s e t , i , j }$ is the weight of business segment j for company i based on the contribution to total company assets.
$n _ { i }$ is the number of business segments of company i.

sections.title_en: Business Segment Exposure scores

blocks.content: The Toxic Emissions & Waste Business Segment Exposure score of a business segment is based on a mapping of the business segment as disclosed by the company to a corresponding business activity. MSCI S&C uses the Standard Industrial Classification (SIC) system along with industry-specific adjustments to define business activities. The score associated with a business activity is used to calculate a Business Segment Exposure score. Each business activity score is determined by a simple average of the Toxicity score, Air Pollutant score, Hazardous Waste score and Radioactivity score of the business activity:
Where:
$T S _ { j }$ is the Toxicity score for business activity j.
Air Pollutant score for business activity j.
Hazardous Waste score for business activity j.
$R S _ { j }$ is the Radioactivity score for business activity j.
The Toxicity score of a business activity is assessed by examining the toxicity and carcinogenicity (oral and inhalation) risk associated with toxic emissions.

The Air Pollutant score of a business activity is assessed by taking a simple average of emissions of carbon monoxide (CO), volatile organic compounds (VOCs), nitrogen oxides (NOx), sulphur oxides (SOx) and particulate matter of 10 micrometer diameter (PM10).
The Hazardous Waste score of a business activity is assessed by examining tons of hazardous waste produced per facility.
The Radioactivity score of a business activity is assessed through a qualitative assessment of the mining industry. Mining activities related to highly radioactive ores receive a score of 10.

sections.title_en: Data sources

blocks.content: The following sources are used to determine the Toxic Emissions & Waste Exposure score:
The EPA’s Toxics Release Inventory, National Emissions Inventory, and Risk-Screening Environmental Indicators; U.S. Economic Census; Refinitiv; MSCI S&C; company disclosures.

## Risks associated with this Key Issue • Increased costs from liabilities associated with damaging health, property. • Loss of access to markets through community opposition, heightened regulatory hurdles. • Increased costs to meet compliance standards and install equipment and systems to contain pollution. ## Toxic Emissions & Waste Key Issue score The Toxic Emissions & Waste Key Issue score evaluates the company’s level of exposure to, and management of, risks on this Key Issue. The Key Issue score is based on the Exposure score and the Management score using the formula below. The Exposure score and the Management score are combined such that a higher level of exposure requires a higher level of demonstrated management capability in order to achieve the same overall Key Issue score. $$ K I _ { i } = 7 - ( \operatorname* { m a x } { ( E X P _ { i } , 2 ) } - M G M T _ { i } ) $$ Where: $K I _ { i }$ is the Key Issue score for company i. $E X P _ { i }$ is the Exposure score for company i. $M G M T _ { i }$ is the Management score for company i. ## Toxic Emissions & Waste Management framework The table below outlines the indicators mapped to their respective components that inform the Toxic Emissions & Waste Management score, excluding controversies. MSCI S&C assigns each indicator a default weight. Indicator weights may be adjusted at the company level to reflect the relevance of the indicator to the company’s business activities. If a company has no exposure to the business activities covered by an indicator, the indicator is assigned a weight of zero.

Expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates strong performance. ## • Three-year average VOC emissions intensity (sales based) Definition: Measures the company’s three-year average VOC emissions per unit of sales. ## ◦ VOC emissions intensity (sales based) industry relative trend score Definition: Assesses the company’s performance on the three-year average of yearover-year VOC emissions (per unit of sales) trend, relative to its peers. Expressed as a 0– 10 score, where 10 indicates strong performance. ## • Three-year average VOC emissions intensity trend (sales based) Definition: Measures the company’s three-year average of year-over-year VOC emissions (per unit of sales) trend. ## • Particulate matter emissions performance relative to peers Definition: Assesses the company's performance on particulate matter (PM) emissions intensity (normalized by sales), and trend in PM emissions intensity), relative to its peers. Expressed as a 0-10 score, where 10 indicates strong performance. ## ◦ Particulate matter emissions intensity industry relative score Definition: Assesses the company’s performance on particulate matter (PM) emissions intensity (emissions per unit of sales) relative to its peers. Expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates strong performance. ## • Three-year average particulate matter emissions intensity (sales based) Definition: Measures the company’s three-year average particulate matter emissions (per unit of sales). ## ◦ Particulate matter emissions intensity industry relative trend score Definition: Assesses the company’s performance on the three-year average of yearover-year particulate matter emissions intensity (per unit of sales) trend, relative to its industry peers. Expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates strong performance. ## • Three-year average particulate matter emissions intensity trend (sales based) Definition: Measures the company’s three-year average of year-over-year particulate matter emissions intensity(per unit of sales) trend. ## • Hazardous waste performance relative to peers Definition: Assesses the company's performance on hazardous waste intensity (normalized by sales), and trend in hazardous waste intensity, relative to its peers. Expressed as a 0-10 score, where 10 indicates strong performance. ## ◦ Hazardous waste intensity industry relative score Definition: Assesses the company’s performance on hazardous waste generated normalized by sales, relative to its industry peers. Expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates strong performance. ## • Three-year average hazardous waste intensity (sales based) Definition: Measures the company’s three-year average hazardous waste generated per unit of sales. ## ◦ Hazardous waste intensity industry relative trend score Definition: Assesses the company’s performance on the three-year average of yearover-year hazardous waste generated (per unit of sales) trend, relative to its industry peers. Expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates strong performance. ## • Three-year average hazardous waste intensity trend (sales based) Definition: Measures the company’s three-year average of year-over-year hazardous waste generated (per unit of sales) trend. ## • Non-hazardous waste performance relative to peers Definition: Assesses the company's performance on non-hazardous waste intensity (normalized by sales), and trend in non-hazardous waste intensity, relative to its peers. Expressed as a 0-10 score, where 10 indicates strong performance. ## ◦ Non-hazardous waste intensity industry relative score Definition: Assesses the company’s performance on non-hazardous waste generated (normalized by sales), relative to its industry peers. Expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates strong performance. ## • Three-year average non-hazardous waste intensity (sales based) Definition: Measures the company’s three-year average non-hazardous waste generated (per unit of sales). ## ◦ Non-hazardous waste intensity industry relative trend score Definition: Assesses the company’s performance on the three-year average of yearover-year non-hazardous generated (per unit of sales) trend, relative to its industry peers. Expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates strong performance. • Three-year average non-hazardous waste intensity trend (sales based) Definition: Measures the company’s three-year average of year-over-year nonhazardous waste generated (per unit of sales) trend. Source: Environmental Protection Agency’s (EPA’s) Resource Conservation and Recovery Act Biennial Reporting. ## Controversies A controversy deduction ranging from 0 to 5 points is subtracted from the overall Management score based on the severity, status, and the company’s role in the controversies facing the company on this Key Issue. The following categories of controversies are used in the assessment: • Toxic emissions and spills controversies. For more details on how controversies are included in the MSCI ESG Ratings model, refer to the Controversies cases section of “ESG Ratings Methodology.” ## Toxic Emissions & Waste Exposure score The Toxic Emissions & Waste Exposure score evaluates the company’s exposure to risks on this Key Issue. It is based on the Business Exposure score only. The Business Exposure score is scored on a 0-10 scale, with 10 corresponding to the highest risk and 0 corresponding to the lowest risk. Refer to the Analyzing risk exposure section of “ESG Ratings Methodology” for additional details. The following formula is used in the Exposure score calculation: $$ E X P _ { T E W , i } = B U S _ { T E W , i } $$ Where: $E X P _ { T E W , i }$ is the Toxic Emissions & Waste Exposure score of company i. $B U S _ { T E W , i }$ is the Toxic Emissions & Waste Business Exposure score of company i. Exhibit 2: Exposure score components 敞口组成图所在官方原件页：有毒排放与废弃物，第14页（图页见本议题结构化正文；官网来源：https://www.msci.com/downloads/documents/access/sustainability-and-climate-resources-and-disclosures/msci-sustainability-and-climate-methodologies/esg-ratings/esg-key-issue-methodologies/environmental-pillar/toxic-emissions-and-waste-key-issue.pdf） ## Business Exposure score The Business Exposure score is a weighted average of the Toxic Emissions & Waste Business Segment Exposure scores of a company’s business segments. scores are weighted by the proportion of a company’s total assets in each business segment,2 using the following formula to calculate the Business Exposure score: $$ B U S _ { T E W , i } = \sum _ { j = 1 } ^ { n _ { i } } w _ { A s s e t , i , j } B S E _ { T E W , j } $$ Where: $B S E _ { T E W , j }$ is the Toxic Emissions & Waste Business Segment Exposure score for business segment j. $w _ { A s s e t , i , j }$ is the weight of business segment j for company i based on the contribution to total company assets. $n _ { i }$ is the number of business segments of company i. ## Business Segment Exposure scores The Toxic Emissions & Waste Business Segment Exposure score of a business segment is based on a mapping of the business segment as disclosed by the company to a corresponding business activity. MSCI S&C uses the Standard Industrial Classification (SIC) system along with industry-specific adjustments to define business activities. The score associated with a business activity is used to calculate a Business Segment Exposure score. Each business activity score is determined by a simple average of the Toxicity score, Air Pollutant score, Hazardous Waste score and Radioactivity score of the business activity: $$ B S E _ { T E W , j } = \frac { T S _ { j } + A P S _ { j } + H W S _ { j } + R S _ { j } } { 4 } $$ Where: $T S _ { j }$ is the Toxicity score for business activity j. Air Pollutant score for business activity j. Hazardous Waste score for business activity j. $R S _ { j }$ is the Radioactivity score for business activity j. The Toxicity score of a business activity is assessed by examining the toxicity and carcinogenicity (oral and inhalation) risk associated with toxic emissions. The Air Pollutant score of a business activity is assessed by taking a simple average of emissions of carbon monoxide (CO), volatile organic compounds (VOCs), nitrogen oxides (NOx), sulphur oxides (SOx) and particulate matter of 10 micrometer diameter (PM10). The Hazardous Waste score of a business activity is assessed by examining tons of hazardous waste produced per facility. The Radioactivity score of a business activity is assessed through a qualitative assessment of the mining industry. Mining activities related to highly radioactive ores receive a score of 10. ## Data sources The following sources are used to determine the Toxic Emissions & Waste Exposure score: The EPA’s Toxics Release Inventory, National Emissions Inventory, and Risk-Screening Environmental Indicators; U.S. Economic Census; Refinitiv; MSCI S&C; company disclosures. ## Contact us ## About MSCI Inc. sections.title_en: Introduction

blocks.content: This document provides essential information on the components of the Packaging Material & Waste Key Issue to enable users of ESG Ratings to understand how MSCI Sustainability & Climate’s (MSCI S&C’s)1 outputs are determined. Packaging Material & Waste is a Key Issue in the Environmental Pillar of the MSCI ESG Ratings model. Companies are evaluated on their production of or reliance upon packaging materials, their potential exposure to waste management and packaging regulations, as well as their efforts to reduce the environmental impact of packaging materials.
For additional details on the MSCI ESG Ratings Model, refer to the Data, ratings and scores section of “ESG Ratings Methodology.”

sections.title_en: Packaging Material & Waste Key Issue score

blocks.content: The Packaging Material & Waste Key Issue score evaluates the company’s level of exposure to, and management of, risks on this Key Issue. The Key Issue score on this Key Issue is based on the Exposure score and the Management score using the formula below. The Exposure score and the Management score are combined such that a higher level of exposure requires a higher level of demonstrated management capability in order to achieve the same overall Key Issue score.

$$
K I _ { i } = 7 - ( \operatorname* { m a x } { ( E X P _ { i } , 2 ) } - M G M T _ { i } )
$$

$E X P _ { i }$ is the Exposure score for company i.
$M G M T _ { i }$ is the Management score for company i.

sections.title_en: Packaging Material & Waste Practices score

blocks.content: The Packaging Material & Waste Practices score evaluates the company’s ability to manage its exposure to risks related to its production of or reliance upon packaging materials, as well as its efforts to reduce the environmental impact of packaging materials. This score is a component of the Packaging Material & Waste Management score (excluding controversies) and considers attributes of the company's policies and initiatives. It is expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates strong initiatives.

sections.title_en: • Disclosure of packaging material mix

blocks.content: Definition: How transparent the company is about the type of materials used in its packaging. Best practice is full disclosure.

sections.title_en: • Scope of consumer programs to reduce waste

blocks.content: Definition: The scope of the company’s consumer education programs on recycling (e.g., take-back locations) or recycling instructions.
• Scope of recycling programs where not mandated by law

Definition: The extent of the company’s involvement in recycling or recovery of packaging materials in locations or circumstances where packaging waste recycling is not mandated by law. Best practice is to have an overarching packaging waste strategy.

sections.title_en: • Strategy to reduce the environmental impact of packaging

blocks.content: Definition: The comprehensiveness of the company’s strategy to reduce the environmental impact of its packaging, such as through waste elimination, packaging redesign, and engagement with suppliers or customers. Best practice is to have specific initiatives that reduce the environmental impact of packaging.

sections.title_en: • Targets related to packaging content

blocks.content: Definition: Assesses the company's targets and their scope focused on recycled material content of packaging. Expressed as a 0-10 score, with 10 indicating strong initiatives.

sections.title_en: ◦ Targets to increase recycled or renewable material content of packaging

blocks.content: Definition: Indicates whether the company has specific targets for improving packaging content, such as increasing recycled content, renewable content, or eliminating problematic or hard-to-recycle plastic content.

blocks.content: Definition: Assesses the company's targets and their scope focused on packaging material circularity or waste elimination. Expressed as a 0-10 score, with 10 indicating strong initiatives.

blocks.content: Definition: Indicates the scope of environmental targets related to material recovery or waste elimination in packaging.

sections.title_en: ◦ Targets for packaging material circularity or waste elimination

sections.title_en: Packaging Material & Waste Performance score

blocks.content: The Packaging Material & Waste Performance score evaluates the company's performance on packaging material & waste metrics (including achievements on packaging content and product recovery). It is expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates the highest level of performance.

sections.title_en: • Scope of environmental improvements in packaging

blocks.content: Definition: Assesses the company's achievements on packaging content (e.g. light-weighted, recycled content).

sections.title_en: • Scope of product or packaging recovery

blocks.content: Definition: Assesses the company's achievements on product or packaging recovery.

sections.title_en: Packaging Material & Waste Exposure score

blocks.content: The Packaging Material & Waste Exposure score evaluates the company’s exposure to risks on this Key Issue. It is based on the Business and Geographic Exposure scores. The Geographic Exposure score functions as a multiplier on the Business Exposure score, with an impact ranging from -50% to +50%. The Business and Geographic Exposure scores are scored on a 0-10 scale, with 10 corresponding to the highest risk and 0 corresponding to the lowest risk. Refer to the Analyzing risk exposure section of “ESG Ratings Methodology” for additional details. The following formula is used in the Exposure score calculation:

$$
E X P _ { P M W , i } = B U S _ { P M W , i } ( 1 + 0 . 1 \big ( G E O _ { P M W , i } - 5 \big ) )
$$
Where:
$E X P _ { P M W , i }$ is the Packaging Material & Waste Exposure score of company i.
$B U S _ { P M W , i }$ is the Business Exposure score of company i.
$G E O _ { P M W , i }$ is the Geographic Exposure score of company i.

Packaging Material & Waste is a Key Issue in the Environmental Pillar of the MSCI ESG Ratings model. Companies are evaluated on their production of or reliance upon packaging materials, their potential exposure to waste management and packaging regulations, as well as their efforts to reduce the environmental impact of packaging materials. For additional details on the MSCI ESG Ratings Model, refer to the Data, ratings and scores section of “ESG Ratings Methodology.” Exhibit 1: MSCI ESG Key Issue hierarchy

## Risks associated with this Key Issue • Loss of access to markets due to reform of regulations governing packaging material and waste. • Loss of revenue due to changing consumer preferences. • Increased costs to reformulate packaging and comply with producer responsibility regulations. ## Packaging Material & Waste Key Issue score The Packaging Material & Waste Key Issue score evaluates the company’s level of exposure to, and management of, risks on this Key Issue. The Key Issue score on this Key Issue is based on the Exposure score and the Management score using the formula below. The Exposure score and the Management score are combined such that a higher level of exposure requires a higher level of demonstrated management capability in order to achieve the same overall Key Issue score. $$ K I _ { i } = 7 - ( \operatorname* { m a x } { ( E X P _ { i } , 2 ) } - M G M T _ { i } ) $$ Where: $K I _ { i }$ is the Key Issue score for company i. $E X P _ { i }$ is the Exposure score for company i. $M G M T _ { i }$ is the Management score for company i. ## Packaging Material & Waste Management framework The table below outlines the indicators mapped to their respective components that inform the Packaging Material & Waste Management score, excluding controversies. MSCI S&C assigns each indicator a default weight. Indicator weights may be adjusted at the company level to reflect the relevance of the indicator to the company’s business activities. If a company has no exposure to the business activities covered by an indicator, the indicator is assigned a weight of zero.
