## Packaging Material & Waste Management score The Packaging Material & Waste Management score evaluates the company’s ability to manage its exposure to risks on this Key Issue. It is based on weighted average of the score associated with each relevant indicator, modified by controversies. This score is derived from indicators that are scored on a 0-10 scale, with 10 corresponding to best practice. Refer to the Analyzing risk management section of “ESG Ratings Methodology” for additional details. Sources are company disclosures except where otherwise indicated. The following formula is used to calculate the Packaging Material & Waste Management score - Excluding Controversies: $$ M G M T _ { i } = \ \sum I n d i c a t o r \_ S c o r e _ { j , i } \ast I n d i c a t o r \_ W e i g h t _ { j , i } $$ Where: $M G M T _ { i }$ is the Management score - Excluding Controversies for company i. $Indicator\_Score_{j,i}$ is the score of indicator j for company i. $Indicator\_Weight_{j,i}$ is the weight of indicator j for company i. The following formula is used to calculate the scores for the components $$ C O M P _ { c , i } = \sum _ { j \in c } I n d i c a t o r \_ S c o r e _ { j , i } * I n d i c a t o r \_ W e i g h t \_ S c a l e d _ { j , i } $$ Where: $C O M P _ { c , i }$ is the component score for component , for company i. $Indicator\_Score_{j,i}$ is the score of indicator j for company i. $Indicator\_Weight\_Scaled_{j,i}$ is the scaled weight of indicator j for company i. $j \in c$ indicates that the summation is over all indicators belonging to component The following formula is used to calculate the weights for the components $$ C O M P \_ W e i g h t _ { c , i } = \sum _ { j \in c } I n d i c a t o r \_ W e i g h t _ { j , i } $$ Where: $C O M P \_ W e i g h t _ { c , i }$ is the component weight for component for company i. $Indicator\_Weight_{j,i}$ is the weight of indicator j for company i. $j \in c$ indicates that the summation is over all indicators belonging to component . The definitions of the data points in each component are given below: ## Packaging Material & Waste Practices score The Packaging Material & Waste Practices score evaluates the company’s ability to manage its exposure to risks related to its production of or reliance upon packaging materials, as well as its efforts to reduce the environmental impact of packaging materials. This score is a component of the Packaging Material & Waste Management score (excluding controversies) and considers attributes of the company's policies and initiatives. It is expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates strong initiatives. ## • Disclosure of packaging material mix Definition: How transparent the company is about the type of materials used in its packaging. Best practice is full disclosure. ## • Scope of consumer programs to reduce waste Definition: The scope of the company’s consumer education programs on recycling (e.g., take-back locations) or recycling instructions. • Scope of recycling programs where not mandated by law Definition: The extent of the company’s involvement in recycling or recovery of packaging materials in locations or circumstances where packaging waste recycling is not mandated by law. Best practice is to have an overarching packaging waste strategy. ## • Strategy to reduce the environmental impact of packaging Definition: The comprehensiveness of the company’s strategy to reduce the environmental impact of its packaging, such as through waste elimination, packaging redesign, and engagement with suppliers or customers. Best practice is to have specific initiatives that reduce the environmental impact of packaging. ## • Targets related to packaging content Definition: Assesses the company's targets and their scope focused on recycled material content of packaging. Expressed as a 0-10 score, with 10 indicating strong initiatives. ## ◦ Scope of targets to increase recycled material content of packaging Definition: Indicates the scope of a company's target to incorporate postconsumer recycled materials into its packaging. ## ◦ Targets to increase recycled or renewable material content of packaging Definition: Indicates whether the company has specific targets for improving packaging content, such as increasing recycled content, renewable content, or eliminating problematic or hard-to-recycle plastic content. ## • Targets related to packaging material circularity or waste elimination Definition: Assesses the company's targets and their scope focused on packaging material circularity or waste elimination. Expressed as a 0-10 score, with 10 indicating strong initiatives. ## ◦ Scope of targets for packaging material circularity or waste elimination Definition: Indicates the scope of environmental targets related to material recovery or waste elimination in packaging. ## ◦ Targets for packaging material circularity or waste elimination Definition: Indicates whether the company has specific targets related to improving product recovery through packaging. ## Packaging Material & Waste Performance score The Packaging Material & Waste Performance score evaluates the company's performance on packaging material & waste metrics (including achievements on packaging content and product recovery). It is expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates the highest level of performance. ## • Scope of environmental improvements in packaging Definition: Assesses the company's achievements on packaging content (e.g. light-weighted, recycled content). ## • Scope of product or packaging recovery Definition: Assesses the company's achievements on product or packaging recovery. ## Controversies A controversy deduction ranging from 0 to 5 points is subtracted from the overall Management score based on the severity, status, and the company’s role in the controversies facing the company on this Key Issue. The following categories of controversies are used in the assessment: ## • Packaging waste controversies. For more details on how controversies are included in the MSCI ESG Ratings model, refer to the Controversies cases section of “ESG Ratings Methodology.” ## Packaging Material & Waste Exposure score The Packaging Material & Waste Exposure score evaluates the company’s exposure to risks on this Key Issue. It is based on the Business and Geographic Exposure scores. The Geographic Exposure score functions as a multiplier on the Business Exposure score, with an impact ranging from -50% to +50%. The Business and Geographic Exposure scores are scored on a 0-10 scale, with 10 corresponding to the highest risk and 0 corresponding to the lowest risk. Refer to the Analyzing risk exposure section of “ESG Ratings Methodology” for additional details. The following formula is used in the Exposure score calculation: $$ E X P _ { P M W , i } = B U S _ { P M W , i } ( 1 + 0 . 1 \big ( G E O _ { P M W , i } - 5 \big ) ) $$ Where: $E X P _ { P M W , i }$ is the Packaging Material & Waste Exposure score of company i. $B U S _ { P M W , i }$ is the Business Exposure score of company i. $G E O _ { P M W , i }$ is the Geographic Exposure score of company i. MSCI S&C uses the Standard Industrial Classification (SIC) system along with industry-specific adjustments to define business activities. The score associated with a business activity is used to calculate a Business Segment Exposure score. Each business activity score is determined by a simple average of the Plastic Packaging Use and Waste Intensity score and the Plastic Packaging Reliance score. $$ B S E _ { P M W , j } = \frac { P P U W S _ { j } + P P R S _ { j } } { 2 } $$ Where: • is the Plastic Packaging Use and Waste Intensity score for business activity j. Plastic Packaging Reliance score for business activity j. The Plastic Packaging Use and Waste Intensity score for each business activity is determined by a combined measure of plastic use and plastic waste intensities in metric tons per million euros of economic output in the business activity. The Plastic Packaging Reliance score for each business activity is determined by a qualitative assessment of whether packaging plays a critical role in the delivery of products and services and whether plastic is a common form of packaging material used. ## Geographic Exposure score The Geographic Exposure score is a weighted average of the Geographic Segment Exposure scores of the countries, markets and regions in which a company operates. scores are weighted by the proportion of a company’s total revenue in each geographic segment through the following equation: $$ G E O _ { P M W , i } = \sum _ { r = 1 } ^ { n _ { i } } w _ { R e v e n u e , i , r } G S E _ { P M W , r } $$ Where: $G S E _ { P M W , r }$ is the Geographic Segment Exposure score of region . $w _ { R e v e n u e , i , r }$ is the weight of total assets in region r for company i. • $n _ { i }$ is the number of geographic segments for company i. For geographic segments disclosed as regions (example: Asia Pacific), a nominal GDP-weighted country or market aggregation is used to calculate region-level scores, using the following equation: $$ G S E _ { P M W , r } = \sum _ { c = 1 } ^ { n _ { r } } w _ { G D P , r , c } G S E _ { P M W , c } $$ Where: $G S E _ { P M W , c }$ is the Geographic Segment Exposure score of country or market . $w _ { G D P , r , c }$ is the specific weight of country or market within region . ## Geographic Segment Exposure scores The Geographic Segment Exposure score is determined by a simple average of the Recycling Mandates score, the Extended Producer Responsibility score, the Single-use Plastic Law score and the Plastic Waste Mismanagement score: $$ G S E _ { P M W , c } = \frac { R M _ { c } + E P R _ { c } + S U P _ { c } + P W M _ { c } } { 2 } $$ Where: $R M _ { c }$ is the Recycling Mandates score in country or market c. $E P R _ { c }$ is the Extended Producer Responsibility score in country or market . $S U P _ { c }$ is the Single-use plastics score in country or market . $P W M _ { c }$ is the Plastic Waste Mismanagement score in country or market . The Recycling Mandates score is based on a country’s recycling mandate policies’ stringency and the extent to which the policies are applied within a country or market. The Extended Producer Responsibility score is based on a country’s extended producer responsibility regulations’ stringency and the extent to which the policies are applied within a country or market. The Single-use Plastic Law score is based on a country’s single-use plastics regulations’ stringency and the extent to which the policies are applied within a country or market. The Plastic Waste Mismanagement score for each country is based on the quantity of plastic waste generated per capita. ## Data sources The following sources are used to determine the Packaging Material & Waste Exposure score: “Plastics Policy Inventory,” Duke University; United Nations Environment Programme, Legal Limits on Single-Use Plastics and Microplastics: A Global Review of National Laws and Regulations; “What A Waste Global Database,” World Bank; Cimpan, C., Bjelle, E.L., and Strømman, A.H., “Plastic packaging flows in Europe: A hybrid input-output approach,” Journal of Industrial Ecology 25, no. 6: 1572-1587; World Development Indicators, World Bank; Refinitiv; MSCI S&C; and company disclosures. ## Contact us ## About MSCI Inc. sections.title_en: Introduction

blocks.content: This document provides essential information on the components of the Electronic Waste Key Issue to enable users of ESG Ratings to understand how MSCI Sustainability & Climate’s (MSCI S&C’s)1 outputs are determined. Electronic Waste is a Key Issue in the Environmental Pillar of the MSCI ESG Ratings model. Companies are evaluated on their production of electronic waste, their potential exposure to electronic waste regulations and their efforts at product collection and recycling.
For additional details on the MSCI ESG Ratings Model, refer to the Data, ratings and scores section of “ESG Ratings Methodology.”

sections.title_en: Electronic Waste Key Issue score

blocks.content: The Electronic Waste Key Issue score evaluates the company’s level of exposure to, and management of, risks on this Key Issue. The Key Issue score on this Key Issue is based on the Exposure score and the Management score using the formula below. The Exposure score and the Management score are combined such that a higher level of exposure requires a higher level of demonstrated management capability in order to achieve the same overall Key Issue score.

$M G M T _ { i }$ is the Management score for company i.

sections.title_en: Electronic Waste Practices score

blocks.content: The Electronic Waste Practices score evaluates the company’s ability to manage risks related to electronic-waste generation, product take-back and recycling programs. This score considers attributes of the company's policies and initiatives. It is expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates strong initiatives.

sections.title_en: • Scope of the electronic waste take-back program by product type

blocks.content: Definition: The scope of products that are eligible for collection and recycling under the company’s electronic waste product recycling program.

sections.title_en: • Scope of the electronic waste take-back program by location

blocks.content: Definition: The geographic scope of the company’s product collection and electronic waste recycling program.

sections.title_en: • Scope of electronic waste take-back programs

blocks.content: Definition: Assesses the company’s return channels for end-of-life products - drop-off, mail-in, and pick-up. Expressed as a 0-10 score, with 10 indicating strong initiatives.

sections.title_en: ◦ Electronic waste take-back programs include drop-off of end-of-life products

blocks.content: Definition: Indicates whether channels for consumers to return end-of-life electronics to the company include drop-off options (at a store or designated drop-off locations).

o Electronic waste take-back programs include mail-in of end-of-life products Definition: Indicates whether available channels for consumers to return end-of-life electronics to the company include mail-in options.

sections.title_en: ◦ Electronic waste take-back programs include pick-up of end-of-life products

blocks.content: Definition: Indicates whether available channels for consumers to return end-of-life electronics to the company include pick-up options.

sections.title_en: ◦ Electronic waste take-back program exists but no details given

blocks.content: Definition Indicates whether channels exist for consumers to return end-of-life electronics to the company, but details are not provided.

sections.title_en: • Facilities that handle recycling of collected electronics

blocks.content:
Definition: Assesses company efforts in managing electronic waste through recycling. 
Expressed as a 0-10 score, with 10 indicating strong initiatives.

sections.title_en: ◦ Company-operated electronic waste recycling facilities

blocks.content: Definition: Indicates whether the company operates its own electronic waste recycling facilities. The company may also use vendors or participate in recycling management organizations for electronic waste recycling.

sections.title_en: ◦ Participation in electronic waste recycling programs

blocks.content: Definition: Indicates that the company participates in electronic waste (e-waste) recycling management organizations (or recycling consortia/network) that support or operate recycling facilities. The company may also operate its own facilities or use vendors for ewaste recycling.

sections.title_en: ◦ Vendor-operated electronic waste recycling facilities

blocks.content: Definition: Indicates that the company uses designated vendors that operate electronic waste (e-waste) recycling facilities. The company may also operate its own facilities or participate in recycling management organizations for e-waste recycling. Moreover, indicates whether these vendors audited or certified by the company or third-party audit programs (including but not limited to R2, e-stewards and WEEELABEX).

sections.title_en: ◦ Unspecified electronic waste recycling activities

blocks.content: Definition: Indicates that the company has a general statement on recycling electronic waste (e-waste) with no further details regarding the facilities, vendors or organizations that handle recycling of collected e-waste.

sections.title_en: • Explicit ban on electronic waste exports to non-OECD countries

blocks.content: Definition: Indicates whether the company explicitly bans electronic waste exports from OECD member countries to non-OECD member countries for disposal and recovery, in accordance with the Basel Ban Amendment to the Basel Convention.

sections.title_en: Electronic Waste Performance score

blocks.content: The Electronic Waste Performance score evaluates the company's performance on electronic waste management metrics (including recycling of electronic waste). It is expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates strong performance.

sections.title_en: • End of life electronic waste recycling

blocks.content: Definition: Assesses the company's performance on the share of electronic waste that is recovered and subsequently recycled by the company. Expressed as a 0-10 score, with 10 indicating strong performance.

sections.title_en: ◦ Percentage of electronic waste recycled – Reported

blocks.content: Definition: Indicates the proportion of collected end-of-life electronic waste that is successfully recycled and repurposed relative to the total end-of-life products and e-waste recovered.
Sources: Company disclosures, Silicon Valley Toxics Coalition, Basel Action Network, GoodElectronics, Greenpeace’s Greener Electronics reports.

sections.title_en: Controversies

blocks.content: A controversy deduction ranging from 0 to 5 points is subtracted from the overall Management score based on the severity, status, and the company’s role in the controversies facing the company on this Key Issue. The following categories of controversies are used in the assessment:

sections.title_en: • Electronic waste controversies.

blocks.content: For more details on how controversies are included in the MSCI ESG Ratings model, refer to the Controversies cases section of “ESG Ratings Methodology.”

sections.title_en: Electronic Waste Exposure score

blocks.content: The Electronic Waste Exposure score evaluates the company’s exposure to risks on this Key Issue. It is based on the Business and Geographic Exposure scores. The Geographic Exposure score functions as a multiplier on the Business Exposure score, with an impact ranging from -50% to +50%. The Business and Geographic Exposure scores are scored on a 0-10 scale, with 10 corresponding to the highest risk and 0 corresponding to the lowest risk. Refer to the Analyzing risk exposure section of “ESG Ratings Methodology” for additional details. The following data sources and methodologies are used in the Exposure score calculation:

$$
E X P _ { E L W , i } = B U S _ { E L W , i } ( 1 + 0 . 1 \big ( G E O _ { E L W , i } - 5 \big ) )
$$
Where:
$E X P _ { E L W , i }$ is the Electronic Waste Exposure score of company i.
$B U S _ { E L W , i }$ is the Business Exposure score of company i.
$G E O _ { E L W , i }$ is the Geographic Exposure score of company i.

sections.title_en: Business Segment Exposure score

blocks.content: The Business Exposure score is a weighted average of the Business Segment Exposure scores of a company’s business segments. scores are weighted by the proportion of a company’s total revenue in each business segment, using the following formula to calculate the Business Exposure score:
Where:
$B S E _ { E L W , j }$ is the Business Segment Exposure score for business segment j.
$w _ { R e v e n u e , i , j }$ is the weight of business segment j for company i based on the contribution to total company revenue.
$n _ { i }$ is the number of business segments of company i.

sections.title_en: Business Segment Exposure scores

blocks.content: The Business Segment Exposure score of a business segment is based on a mapping of the business segment as disclosed by the company to a corresponding business activity. MSCI S&C uses the Standard Industrial Classification (SIC) system along with industry-specific adjustments to define business activities. The score associated with a business activity is used to calculate a Business Segment Exposure score. Each business activity score is determined by a weighted average of the Type of Operations score and Type of Product score:

$$
B S E _ { E L W , j } = 0 . 3 5 \bigl ( T O O _ { E L W , j } \bigr ) + 0 . 6 5 ( T O P _ { E L W , j } )
$$
Where:
$T O O _ { E L W , j }$ is the Type of Operations score for business activity j.
$T O P _ { E L W , j }$ is the Type of Product score for business activity j.
The Type of Operations score is assessed as a qualitative assessment of whether the type of operations of a business activity involves the manufacture and/or sale of electronic equipment and devices.

The Type of Product score is assessed as a qualitative assessment of whether the product category of the business activity involves the manufacture and/or sale of electronic equipment and devices. The product categories considered are consumer electronics, office electronics, household appliances and professional equipment.

sections.title_en: Geographic Exposure score

blocks.content: The Geographic Exposure score is a weighted average of the Geographic Segment Exposure scores of the countries,markets and regions in which the company operates. scores are weighted by the proportion of the company’s total revenue in each geographic segment through the following equation:
Where:
$G S E _ { E L W , r }$ is the Geographic Segment Exposure score in region .
$w _ { R e v e n u e , i , r }$ is the weight of region r for company i based on the contribution to total company revenue.
$n _ { i }$ is the number of geographic segments for company i.
For geographic segments disclosed as regions (example: Asia Pacific), a nominal GDP-weighted country or market aggregation is used to calculate region-level scores, using the following equation:
Where:
$G S E _ { E L W , c }$ is the Geographic Segment Exposure score of country or market .
$w _ { G D P , r , c }$ is the specific weight of country or market within region .

sections.title_en: Geographic Segment Exposure scores

blocks.content: The Geographic Segment Exposure score is determined by a qualitative framework to assess countries or markets with strengthening or evolving electronic waste regulations. Higher regulation standards and wider coverage result in a higher risk exposure score for a given country or market.

It is expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates strong initiatives. ## • Scope of the electronic waste take-back program by product type Definition: The scope of products that are eligible for collection and recycling under the company’s electronic waste product recycling program. ## • Scope of the electronic waste take-back program by location Definition: The geographic scope of the company’s product collection and electronic waste recycling program. ## • Scope of electronic waste take-back programs Definition: Assesses the company’s return channels for end-of-life products - drop-off, mail-in, and pick-up. Expressed as a 0-10 score, with 10 indicating strong initiatives. ## ◦ Electronic waste take-back programs include drop-off of end-of-life products Definition: Indicates whether channels for consumers to return end-of-life electronics to the company include drop-off options (at a store or designated drop-off locations). o Electronic waste take-back programs include mail-in of end-of-life products Definition: Indicates whether available channels for consumers to return end-of-life electronics to the company include mail-in options. ## ◦ Electronic waste take-back programs include pick-up of end-of-life products Definition: Indicates whether available channels for consumers to return end-of-life electronics to the company include pick-up options. ## ◦ Electronic waste take-back program exists but no details given Definition Indicates whether channels exist for consumers to return end-of-life electronics to the company, but details are not provided. ## • Facilities that handle recycling of collected electronics Definition: Assesses company efforts in managing electronic waste through recycling. Expressed as a 0-10 score, with 10 indicating strong initiatives. ## ◦ Company-operated electronic waste recycling facilities Definition: Indicates whether the company operates its own electronic waste recycling facilities. The company may also use vendors or participate in recycling management organizations for electronic waste recycling. ## ◦ Participation in electronic waste recycling programs Definition: Indicates that the company participates in electronic waste (e-waste) recycling management organizations (or recycling consortia/network) that support or operate recycling facilities. The company may also operate its own facilities or use vendors for ewaste recycling. ## ◦ Vendor-operated electronic waste recycling facilities Definition: Indicates that the company uses designated vendors that operate electronic waste (e-waste) recycling facilities. The company may also operate its own facilities or participate in recycling management organizations for e-waste recycling. Moreover, indicates whether these vendors audited or certified by the company or third-party audit programs (including but not limited to R2, e-stewards and WEEELABEX). ## ◦ Unspecified electronic waste recycling activities Definition: Indicates that the company has a general statement on recycling electronic waste (e-waste) with no further details regarding the facilities, vendors or organizations that handle recycling of collected e-waste. ## • Explicit ban on electronic waste exports to non-OECD countries Definition: Indicates whether the company explicitly bans electronic waste exports from OECD member countries to non-OECD member countries for disposal and recovery, in accordance with the Basel Ban Amendment to the Basel Convention. ## Electronic Waste Performance score The Electronic Waste Performance score evaluates the company's performance on electronic waste management metrics (including recycling of electronic waste). It is expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates strong performance. ## • End of life electronic waste recycling Definition: Assesses the company's performance on the share of electronic waste that is recovered and subsequently recycled by the company. Expressed as a 0-10 score, with 10 indicating strong performance. ## ◦ Percentage of electronic waste recycled – Reported Definition: Indicates the proportion of collected end-of-life electronic waste that is successfully recycled and repurposed relative to the total end-of-life products and e-waste recovered. Sources: Company disclosures, Silicon Valley Toxics Coalition, Basel Action Network, GoodElectronics, Greenpeace’s Greener Electronics reports. ## Controversies A controversy deduction ranging from 0 to 5 points is subtracted from the overall Management score based on the severity, status, and the company’s role in the controversies facing the company on this Key Issue. The following categories of controversies are used in the assessment: ## • Electronic waste controversies. For more details on how controversies are included in the MSCI ESG Ratings model, refer to the Controversies cases section of “ESG Ratings Methodology.” ## Electronic Waste Exposure score The Electronic Waste Exposure score evaluates the company’s exposure to risks on this Key Issue. It is based on the Business and Geographic Exposure scores. The Geographic Exposure score functions as a multiplier on the Business Exposure score, with an impact ranging from -50% to +50%. The Business and Geographic Exposure scores are scored on a 0-10 scale, with 10 corresponding to the highest risk and 0 corresponding to the lowest risk. Refer to the Analyzing risk exposure section of “ESG Ratings Methodology” for additional details. The following data sources and methodologies are used in the Exposure score calculation: $$ E X P _ { E L W , i } = B U S _ { E L W , i } ( 1 + 0 . 1 \big ( G E O _ { E L W , i } - 5 \big ) ) $$ Where: $E X P _ { E L W , i }$ is the Electronic Waste Exposure score of company i. $B U S _ { E L W , i }$ is the Business Exposure score of company i. $G E O _ { E L W , i }$ is the Geographic Exposure score of company i. Exhibit 2: Exposure score components 敞口组成图所在官方原件页：电子废弃物，第9页（图页见本议题结构化正文；官网来源：https://www.msci.com/downloads/documents/access/sustainability-and-climate-resources-and-disclosures/msci-sustainability-and-climate-methodologies/esg-ratings/esg-key-issue-methodologies/environmental-pillar/electronic-waste-key-issue.pdf） ## Business Segment Exposure score The Business Exposure score is a weighted average of the Business Segment Exposure scores of a company’s business segments. scores are weighted by the proportion of a company’s total revenue in each business segment, using the following formula to calculate the Business Exposure score: $$ B U S _ { E L W , i } = { \sum } _ { j = 1 } ^ { n _ { i } } w _ { R e v e n u e , i , j } B S E _ { E L W , j } $$ Where: $B S E _ { E L W , j }$ is the Business Segment Exposure score for business segment j. $w _ { R e v e n u e , i , j }$ is the weight of business segment j for company i based on the contribution to total company revenue. $n _ { i }$ is the number of business segments of company i. ## Business Segment Exposure scores The Business Segment Exposure score of a business segment is based on a mapping of the business segment as disclosed by the company to a corresponding business activity. MSCI S&C uses the Standard Industrial Classification (SIC) system along with industry-specific adjustments to define business activities. The score associated with a business activity is used to calculate a Business Segment Exposure score. Each business activity score is determined by a weighted average of the Type of Operations score and Type of Product score: $$ B S E _ { E L W , j } = 0 . 3 5 \bigl ( T O O _ { E L W , j } \bigr ) + 0 . 6 5 ( T O P _ { E L W , j } ) $$ Where: $T O O _ { E L W , j }$ is the Type of Operations score for business activity j. $T O P _ { E L W , j }$ is the Type of Product score for business activity j. The Type of Operations score is assessed as a qualitative assessment of whether the type of operations of a business activity involves the manufacture and/or sale of electronic equipment and devices. The Type of Product score is assessed as a qualitative assessment of whether the product category of the business activity involves the manufacture and/or sale of electronic equipment and devices. The product categories considered are consumer electronics, office electronics, household appliances and professional equipment. ## Geographic Exposure score The Geographic Exposure score is a weighted average of the Geographic Segment Exposure scores of the countries,markets and regions in which the company operates. scores are weighted by the proportion of the company’s total revenue in each geographic segment through the following equation: $$ G E O _ { E L W , i } = \sum _ { r = 1 } ^ { n _ { i } } w _ { R e v e n u e , i , r } G S E _ { E L W , r } $$ Where: $G S E _ { E L W , r }$ is the Geographic Segment Exposure score in region . $w _ { R e v e n u e , i , r }$ is the weight of region r for company i based on the contribution to total company revenue. $n _ { i }$ is the number of geographic segments for company i. For geographic segments disclosed as regions (example: Asia Pacific), a nominal GDP-weighted country or market aggregation is used to calculate region-level scores, using the following equation: $$ G S E _ { E L W , r } = \sum _ { c = 1 } ^ { n _ { r } } w _ { G D P , r , c } G S E _ { E L W , c } $$ Where: $G S E _ { E L W , c }$ is the Geographic Segment Exposure score of country or market . $w _ { G D P , r , c }$ is the specific weight of country or market within region . ## Geographic Segment Exposure scores The Geographic Segment Exposure score is determined by a qualitative framework to assess countries or markets with strengthening or evolving electronic waste regulations. Higher regulation standards and wider coverage result in a higher risk exposure score for a given country or market. ## Data sources The following sources are used to determine the Electronic Waste Exposure score: Refinitiv, MSCI S&C, company disclosures. ## Contact us ## About MSCI Inc. sections.title_en: Introduction

blocks.content: This document provides essential information on the components of the Opportunities in Clean Tech Key Issue to enable users of ESG Ratings to understand how MSCI Sustainability & Climate’s (MSCI S&C’s)1 outputs are determined. Opportunities in Clean Tech is a Key Issue in the Environmental Pillar of the MSCI ESG Ratings model. Companies are evaluated on their positioning to meet market demand for products with environmental benefits.
For additional details on the MSCI ESG Ratings Model, refer to the Data, ratings and scores section of “ESG Ratings Methodology.”

sections.title_en: Opportunities in Clean Tech Key Issue score

blocks.content: The Opportunities in Clean Tech Key Issue score evaluates the company’s level of exposure to, and management of, opportunities on this Key Issue. The Key Issue score is based on the Exposure score and the Management score using the formula below. The Exposure score and the Management score are combined such that the Exposure score determines the weight placed on the Management score, ranging from 50% (when Exposure score is equal to zero) to 100% (when Exposure score is equal to 10).

$$
K I _ { i } = \left( \left( \frac { E X P _ { i } } { 2 0 } + . 5 \right) \times M G M T _ { i } S c o r e \right) + \left( \left( . 5 - \frac { E X P _ { i } } { 2 0 } \right) \times 5 \right)
$$
Where:
$K I _ { i }$ is the Key Issue score for company i.
$E X P _ { i }$ is the Exposure score for company i.
$M G M T _ { i }$ is the Management score for company i.

sections.title_en: Opportunities in Clean Tech Strategy score

blocks.content: The Opportunities in Clean Tech Strategy score evaluates the company’s initiatives to embed clean technology into its long-term strategy through business focus, R&D direction, and investment targets. It is expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates strong initiatives.

sections.title_en: • Targets to increase investment in clean tech

blocks.content: Definition: Indicates whether the company has disclosed quantitative targets to increase investment in clean technology.

sections.title_en: • Strategic focus on clean technology development

blocks.content: Definition: Assesses the company’s strategic commitment to clean technology as part of its core business focus and growth plans. Highest performance reflects clean technology being a core business line or a primary focus for future R&D and innovation. Expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates the highest level of performance.

sections.title_en: Opportunities in Clean Tech Programs & Initiatives score

blocks.content: The Opportunities in Clean Tech Programs & Initiatives score evaluates the company’s initiatives to advance clean technology through research and development. It is expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates strong initiatives.
• Research and development intensity (as percentage of sales) score

Definition: Assesses the company’s performance on R&D intensity metrics (including R&D intensity normalized by sales, and trend in R&D intensity) relative to its peers. Expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates the highest level of performance.

A business segment's Research and Development Expense score is assessed using the ratio of research and development expenses to revenues at the business activity level. The Research and Development Expense score is scored on a 0-10 scale, with 10 corresponding to the highest research and development expenses per unit of revenue and 0 corresponding to the lowest research and development expenses per unit of revenue.

The Contribution of Opportunities in Clean Tech score of a business activity is assessed using a qualitative assessment based on predefined guidance to determine whether the business activity is a major contributor to opportunities in clean technology. Segments which are major contributors receive a score of 10. Segments with no potential opportunities in clean technology receive a score of 0.

## Opportunities associated with this Key Issue • Increased access to markets due to regulatory reforms and incentives. • Increased revenue from capturing changing demand, early-mover advantage. ## Opportunities in Clean Tech Key Issue score The Opportunities in Clean Tech Key Issue score evaluates the company’s level of exposure to, and management of, opportunities on this Key Issue. The Key Issue score is based on the Exposure score and the Management score using the formula below. The Exposure score and the Management score are combined such that the Exposure score determines the weight placed on the Management score, ranging from 50% (when Exposure score is equal to zero) to 100% (when Exposure score is equal to 10). $$ K I _ { i } = \left( \left( \frac { E X P _ { i } } { 2 0 } + . 5 \right) \times M G M T _ { i } S c o r e \right) + \left( \left( . 5 - \frac { E X P _ { i } } { 2 0 } \right) \times 5 \right) $$ Where: $K I _ { i }$ is the Key Issue score for company i. $E X P _ { i }$ is the Exposure score for company i. $M G M T _ { i }$ is the Management score for company i. ## Opportunities in Clean Tech Management framework The table below outlines the indicators mapped to their respective components that inform the Opportunities in Clean Tech Management score. MSCI S&C assigns each indicator a default weight. Indicator weights may be adjusted at the company level to reflect the relevance of the indicator to the company’s business activities. If a company has no exposure to the business activities covered by an indicator, the indicator is assigned a weight of zero.

## Opportunities in Clean Tech Management score The Opportunities in Clean Tech Management score evaluates the company’s ability to manage its exposure to opportunities on this Key Issue. It is based on weighted average of the score associated with each relevant indicator. This score is derived from indicators that are scored on a 0-10 scale, with 10 corresponding to best practice. Refer to the Analyzing risk management section of “ESG Ratings Methodology” for additional details. Sources are company disclosures except where otherwise indicated. The following formula is used to calculate the Opportunities in Clean Tech Management score: $$ M G M T _ { i } = \ \sum I n d i c a t o r \_ S c o r e _ { j , i } \ast I n d i c a t o r \_ W e i g h t _ { j , i } $$ Where: $M G M T _ { i }$ is the Management score - Excluding Controversies for company i. $Indicator\_Score_{j,i}$ is the score of indicator j for company i. $Indicator\_Weight_{j,i}$ is the weight of indicator j for company i. The following formula is used to calculate the scores for the components $$ C O M P _ { c , i } = \sum _ { j \in c } I n d i c a t o r \_ S c o r e _ { j , i } * I n d i c a t o r \_ W e i g h t \_ S c a l e d _ { j , i } $$ Where: $C O M P _ { c , i }$ is the component score for component $c _ { \prime }$ for company $i .$ $I n d i c a t o r \_ S c o r e _ { j , i }$ is the score of indicator for company . $Indicator\_Weight\_Scaled_{j,i}$ is the scaled weight of indicator j for company i. • j ∈ c indicates that the summation is over all indicators belonging to component The following formula is used to calculate the weights for the components $$ C O M P \_ W e i g h t _ { c , i } = \sum _ { j \in c } I n d i c a t o r \_ W e i g h t _ { j , i } $$ Where: $COMP\_Weight_{c,i}$ is the component weight for component c for company i. $Indicator\_Weight_{j,i}$ is the weight of indicator j for company i. $j \in c$ indicates that the summation is over all indicators belonging to component . The definitions of the data points in each component are given below: ## Opportunities in Clean Tech Strategy score The Opportunities in Clean Tech Strategy score evaluates the company’s initiatives to embed clean technology into its long-term strategy through business focus, R&D direction, and investment targets. It is expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates strong initiatives. ## • Targets to increase investment in clean tech Definition: Indicates whether the company has disclosed quantitative targets to increase investment in clean technology. ## • Strategic focus on clean technology development Definition: Assesses the company’s strategic commitment to clean technology as part of its core business focus and growth plans. Highest performance reflects clean technology being a core business line or a primary focus for future R&D and innovation. Expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates the highest level of performance. ## Opportunities in Clean Tech Programs & Initiatives score The Opportunities in Clean Tech Programs & Initiatives score evaluates the company’s initiatives to advance clean technology through research and development. It is expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates strong initiatives. • Research and development intensity (as percentage of sales) score Definition: Assesses the company’s performance on R&D intensity metrics (including R&D intensity normalized by sales, and trend in R&D intensity) relative to its peers. Expressed as a 0-10 score, where 10 indicates that the company derives more than 50% of its revenue from clean technology products and services. ## Opportunities in Clean Tech Exposure score The Opportunities in Clean Tech Exposure score evaluates the company’s exposure to opportunities on this Key Issue. It is based on the Business Exposure score only. The Business Exposure score is scored on a 0-10 scale, with 10 corresponding to the highest opportunity and 0 corresponding to the lowest opportunity. Refer to the Analyzing risk exposure section of “ESG Ratings Methodology” for additional details. The following formula is used in the Exposure score calculation: $$ E X P _ { O C T , i } = B U S _ { O C T , i } $$ Where: $E X P _ { O C T , i }$ is the Opportunities in Clean Tech Exposure score of company i. $B U S _ { O C T , i }$ is the Business Exposure score of company i. ## Exhibit 2: Exposure score components 敞口组成图所在官方原件页：清洁技术机遇，第8页（图页见本议题结构化正文；官网来源：https://www.msci.com/downloads/documents/access/sustainability-and-climate-resources-and-disclosures/msci-sustainability-and-climate-methodologies/esg-ratings/esg-key-issue-methodologies/environmental-pillar/opportunities-in-clean-tech-key-issue.pdf） ## Business Exposure score The Business Exposure score is a weighted average of the Business Segment Exposure scores of a company’s business segments. scores are weighted by the proportion of a company’s total revenue in each business segment, using the following formula to calculate the Business Exposure score: $$ B U S _ { O C T , i } = \sum _ { j = 1 } ^ { n _ { i } } w _ { R e v e n u e , i , j } B S E _ { O C T , j } $$ Where: $B S E _ { O C T , j }$ is the Business Segment Exposure score for business segment j. $w _ { R e v e n u e , i , j }$ is the weight of business segment j for company i based on the the contribution to total company revenue. $n _ { i }$ is the number of business segments of company i. ## Business Segment Exposure score The Business Segment Exposure score of a business segment is based on a mapping of the business segment as disclosed by the company to a corresponding business activity. sections.title_en: Opportunities in Green Building Key Issue score

blocks.content: The Opportunities in Green Building Key Issue score evaluates the company’s level of exposure to, and management of, opportunities on this Key Issue. The Key Issue score is based on the Exposure score and the Management score using the formula below. The Exposure score and the Management score are combined such that the Exposure score determines the weight placed on the Management score, ranging from 50% (when the Exposure score is equal to zero) to 100% (when the Exposure score is equal to 10).

$$
K I _ { i } = \left( \left( { \frac { E X P _ { i } } { 2 0 } } + 0 . 5 \right) * M G M T _ { i } \right) + \left( \left( 0 . 5 - { \frac { E X P _ { i } } { 2 0 } } \right) * 5 \right)
$$
Where:
$K I _ { i }$ is the Key Issue score for company i.
$E X P _ { i }$ is the Exposure score for company i.
$M G M T _ { i }$ is the Management score for company i.

sections.title_en: Opportunities in Green Building Practices score

blocks.content: The Opportunities in Green Building Practices score evaluates the company’s ability to manage its exposure to opportunities related to the resource consumption and carbon intensity of its property assets and its efforts to improve the environmental performance of its real estate assets. This score is a component of the Opportunities in Green Building Management score and considers attributes of the company's policies and initiatives. It is expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates strong initiatives.

sections.title_en: • Extent of green building certification commitments in portfolio or development pipeline

blocks.content: Definition: The portion of the company’s portfolio or development projects that are covered by its green building commitments. Applies to real estate companies only.

sections.title_en: • Extent of commercial arrangements to improve or maintain property environmental performance

blocks.content: Definition: Indicates whether the company provides evidence of implementing commercial agreements to incentivize tenants and property managers to improve property environmental performance. Applies to real estate companies only.

sections.title_en: • Use of green or triple-net leases

blocks.content: Definition: Indicates whether the company provides evidence of implementing green leases or triple-net leases in its tenancies. Applies to real estate companies only.

sections.title_en: • Green certification commitments related to greenfield developments

blocks.content: Definition: The company’s green building strategy for greenfield sites, including whether there is a clear statement on avoiding greenfield sites, the company only develops green-certified properties on greenfield developments, or we found no evidence of green certification for greenfield developments. Applies to real estate companies only.

sections.title_en: • Evidence of flexible or mixed-use properties in portfolio

blocks.content: Definition: Indicates whether the company provides evidence of flexible or mixed-use properties in its property portfolio. Applies to real estate companies only.

sections.title_en: • Evidence of urban revitalization developments

blocks.content: Definition: The level of urban redevelopment that the company undertakes. Best practice is urban revitalization. Applies to real estate companies only.

sections.title_en: • Green building commitment extends to existing buildings in portfolio (in addition to new buildings)

blocks.content: Definition: Indicates whether the company renovates or redevelops its existing properties with either green building initiatives or green building certifications. Applies to real estate companies only.

sections.title_en: Opportunities in Green Building Performance score

blocks.content: The Opportunities in Green Building Performance score evaluates the company’s performance on opportunities in green building metrics (including percentage of green-certified buildings and space, and carbon emissions ) relative to its peers. It is expressed as a 0-10 score, where 10 indicates the highest level of performance.
The following provides a non-exhaustive overview of the indicators and sub-indicators used in the assessment of the Opportunities in Green Building Performance score.

sections.title_en: • Green building certification score

blocks.content: Definition: Assesses the extent of certified spaces or buildings under selected green building standards. Expressed as a 0-10 score, with 10 indicating highest level of certification coverage across the portfolio.

sections.title_en: ◦ Score of green certified buildings as % of total

blocks.content: Definition: Assesses the company’s performance on the share of green-certified buildings within its real estate portfolio, calculated as the percentage of total buildings that hold recognized green building certifications. Expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates the highest level of performance.

sections.title_en: ◦ Score of green certified space as % of total

blocks.content: Definition: Assesses the company’s performance on the share of green-certified space within its real estate portfolio, calculated as the percentage of total floor area that holds recognized green building certifications. Expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates the highest level of performance.

sections.title_en: ◦ Evidence of green certified buildings in real estate portfolio

blocks.content: Definition: Assesses the extent to which the company provides verifiable evidence of green-certified buildings within its real estate portfolio, based on the availability and quality of supporting documentation such as certification records or third-party registries. Expressed as a 0–5 score, where 10 indicates comprehensive and verifiable evidence.

sections.title_en: • Carbon emissions performance relative to peers

blocks.content: Definition: Assesses the company's performance on greenhouse gas [GHG] emissions intensity (normalized by sales or by units of production), and trend in GHG emissions intensity, relative to its peers. Expressed as a 0-10 score, where 10 indicates the highest level of performance.

sections.title_en: Opportunities in Green Building Exposure score

blocks.content: The Opportunities in Green Building Exposure score evaluates the company’s exposure to opportunities on this Key Issue. It is based on the Business and Geographic Exposure scores. The Geographic Exposure score functions as a multiplier on the Business Exposure score, with an impact ranging from - 50% to +50%. The Business and Geographic Exposure scores are scored on a 0-10 scale, with 10 corresponding to the highest opportunity and 0 corresponding to the lowest opportunity. Refer to the Analyzing risk exposure section of “ESG Ratings Methodology” for additional details. The following formula is used in the Exposure score calculation:

$$
E X P _ { O G B , i } = B U S _ { O G B , i } ( 1 + 0 . 1 \big ( G E O _ { O G B , i } - 5 \big ) )
$$
Where:
$E X P _ { O G B , i }$ is the Opportunities in Green Building Exposure score of company i.
$B U S _ { O G B , i }$ is the Business Exposure score of company i.
$G E O _ { O G B , i }$ is the Geographic Exposure score of company i.

sections.title_en: Business Exposure score

blocks.content: The Business Exposure score is a weighted average of the Business Segment Exposure scores of a company’s business segments. scores are weighted by the proportion of a company’s total revenue in each business segment, using the following formula to calculate the Business Exposure score:
Where:
$B S E _ { O G B , j }$ is the Business Segment Exposure score for business segment j.
$w _ { R e v e n u e , i , j }$ is the weight of business segment j for company i based on the contribution to total company revenue.
$n _ { i }$ is the number of business segments of company i.

sections.title_en: Business Segment Exposure score

blocks.content: The Business Segment Exposure score of a business segment is based on a mapping of the business segment as disclosed by the company to a corresponding business activity. MSCI S&C uses the Standard Industrial Classification (SIC) system along with industry-specific adjustments to define business activities. The score associated with a business activity is used to calculate a Business Segment Exposure score. Each business activity score is determined by a weighted average of the Energy Use Intensity score, Energy Certification score and Water Use Intensity score of the activity.
Where:
$E C _ { j }$ is the Energy Certification score for business activity j.
$E U I _ { j }$ is the Energy Use Intensity score for business activity j.
$W U I _ { j }$ is the Water Use Intensity score for business activity j.
The Energy Certification score for a given business activity is based on the proportion of total building area that is certified to the ENERGY STAR certification for buildings.
The Energy Use Intensity score is based on the aggregate energy use intensity for each business activity in thousands of British thermal units per square foot.
The Water Use Intensity score is based on the volume of water used for each business activity in gallons per square foot. A score of 10 indicates the highest opportunity.

sections.title_en: Geographic Exposure score

blocks.content: The Geographic Exposure score is a weighted average of the Geographic Segment Exposure scores of the countries, markets and regions in which a company operates. Scores are weighted by the proportion of a company’s total revenue in each geographic segment through the following equation:
Where:
$G S E _ { O G B , r }$ is the Geographic Segment Exposure score of region .
$w _ { R e v e n u e , i , r }$ is the weight of total revenue in region r for company i.
$n _ { i }$ is the number of geographic segments for company i.
For geographic segments disclosed as regions (example: Asia Pacific), a nominal GDP-weighted country or market aggregation is used to calculate region-level scores, using the following equation:
Where:
$G S E _ { O G B , c }$ is the Geographic Segment Exposure score of country or market .
$w _ { G D P , r , c }$ is the specific weight of country or market within region .

sections.title_en: Geographic Segment Exposure scores

blocks.content: Countries with strengthening energy and climate change regulations influence the adoption of green buildings. Therefore, the Geographic Segment Exposure score for a country is determined by the reduction in greenhouse gas emissions required per year to meet its publicly disclosed greenhouse gas emissions targets.

$$
G S E _ { O G B , c } = A v g ( N T A _ { c } , L T A _ { c } , G M M _ { c } )
$$
Where:
$N T A _ { c } ,$ is the near-term ambition score of country or market .
$L T A _ { c }$ is the long-term ambition score of country or market .
$G M M _ { c }$ is the government and market mechanisms score of country or market .

The near-term ambition of a country is assessed by considering the annual emissions reduction rate needed to meet their publicly disclosed near-term climate targets. Countries with aggressive near-term targets have high emissions reduction rates and therefore a higher policy pressure segment score.

A country or market’s long-term ambition indicates the strength and credibility of its long-term climate targets such as net-zero commitments. Long term targets could signal the direction of future policy and regulatory developments, even in the near term.
The government and market mechanisms score indicates the current strength of policy and marketbased mechanisms signaling a government’s commitment to driving the energy transition.
This score is calculated as the average of carbon pricing score and fossil fuel subsidies score.

$$
G M M _ { c } = A v g \left( \mathit { C P M } , \mathit { F F S } \right)
$$
Where
Carbon Pricing Mechanisms score
Fossil Fuel Subsidies score.
Carbon pricing mechanisms score indicates mechanisms such as carbon taxes or emissions trading systems that exert policy pressure on companies by assigning a direct cost to carbon emissions.

The fossil fuel subsidies score indicates the degree of financial support for fossil fuel consumption. Lower subsidies (higher scores) increase transition pressure by removing cost advantages, whereas high subsidies (lower scores) signal continued alignment with fossil fuel-based economic structures, thus reducing policy pressure

In the absence of evidence from data sources indicating that a country has near- or long-term emissions reduction targets or carbon pricing mechanisms in place, a score of 0 is assigned. In the absence of a country’s fossil fuel subsidy information, a score of 5 is assigned.

sections.title_en: Data sources

blocks.content: The following sources are used to determine the Opportunities in Green Building Exposure score:

International Monetary Fund (IMF) Implied Mitigation Targets, Net Zero Tracker, Carbon Pricing Dashboard, IMF Fossil Fuel subsidies data; Department of Energy; ENERGY STAR Portfolio Manager, Environmental Protection Agency; Refinitiv; MSCI S&C; company disclosures.

Refer to the Analyzing risk exposure section of “ESG Ratings Methodology” for additional details. The following formula is used in the Exposure score calculation: $$ E X P _ { O G B , i } = B U S _ { O G B , i } ( 1 + 0 . 1 \big ( G E O _ { O G B , i } - 5 \big ) ) $$ Where: $E X P _ { O G B , i }$ is the Opportunities in Green Building Exposure score of company i. $B U S _ { O G B , i }$ is the Business Exposure score of company i. $G E O _ { O G B , i }$ is the Geographic Exposure score of company i. Exhibit 2: Exposure score components 敞口组成图所在官方原件页：绿色建筑机遇，第9页（图页见本议题结构化正文；官网来源：https://www.msci.com/downloads/documents/access/sustainability-and-climate-resources-and-disclosures/msci-sustainability-and-climate-methodologies/esg-ratings/esg-key-issue-methodologies/environmental-pillar/opportunities-in-green-building-key-issue.pdf） ## Business Exposure score The Business Exposure score is a weighted average of the Business Segment Exposure scores of a company’s business segments. scores are weighted by the proportion of a company’s total revenue in each business segment, using the following formula to calculate the Business Exposure score: $$ B U S _ { O G B , i } = \sum _ { j = 1 } ^ { n _ { i } } w _ { R e v e n u e , i , j } B S E _ { O G B , j } $$ Where: $B S E _ { O G B , j }$ is the Business Segment Exposure score for business segment j. $w _ { R e v e n u e , i , j }$ is the weight of business segment j for company i based on the contribution to total company revenue. $n _ { i }$ is the number of business segments of company i. ## Business Segment Exposure score The Business Segment Exposure score of a business segment is based on a mapping of the business segment as disclosed by the company to a corresponding business activity. MSCI S&C uses the Standard Industrial Classification (SIC) system along with industry-specific adjustments to define business activities. The score associated with a business activity is used to calculate a Business Segment Exposure score. Each business activity score is determined by a weighted average of the Energy Use Intensity score, Energy Certification score and Water Use Intensity score of the activity. $$ B S E _ { O G B , j } = 0 . 5 E C _ { j } + 0 . 4 E U I _ { j } + 0 . 1 W U I _ { j } $$ Where: $E C _ { j }$ is the Energy Certification score for business activity j. $E U I _ { j }$ is the Energy Use Intensity score for business activity j. $W U I _ { j }$ is the Water Use Intensity score for business activity j. The Energy Certification score for a given business activity is based on the proportion of total building area that is certified to the ENERGY STAR certification for buildings. The Energy Use Intensity score is based on the aggregate energy use intensity for each business activity in thousands of British thermal units per square foot. The Water Use Intensity score is based on the volume of water used for each business activity in gallons per square foot. A score of 10 indicates the highest opportunity. ## Geographic Exposure score The Geographic Exposure score is a weighted average of the Geographic Segment Exposure scores of the countries, markets and regions in which a company operates. Scores are weighted by the proportion of a company’s total revenue in each geographic segment through the following equation: $$ G E O _ { O G B , i } = \sum _ { r = 1 } ^ { n _ { i } } w _ { R e v e n u e , i , r } G S E _ { O G B , r } $$ Where: $G S E _ { O G B , r }$ is the Geographic Segment Exposure score of region . $w _ { R e v e n u e , i , r }$ is the weight of total revenue in region r for company i. $n _ { i }$ is the number of geographic segments for company i. For geographic segments disclosed as regions (example: Asia Pacific), a nominal GDP-weighted country or market aggregation is used to calculate region-level scores, using the following equation: $$ G S E _ { O G B , r } = \sum _ { c = 1 } ^ { n _ { r } } w _ { G D P , r , c } G S E _ { O G B , c } $$ Where: $G S E _ { O G B , c }$ is the Geographic Segment Exposure score of country or market . $w _ { G D P , r , c }$ is the specific weight of country or market within region . ## Geographic Segment Exposure scores Countries with strengthening energy and climate change regulations influence the adoption of green buildings. Therefore, the Geographic Segment Exposure score for a country is determined by the reduction in greenhouse gas emissions required per year to meet its publicly disclosed greenhouse gas emissions targets. $$ G S E _ { O G B , c } = A v g ( N T A _ { c } , L T A _ { c } , G M M _ { c } ) $$ Where: $N T A _ { c } ,$ is the near-term ambition score of country or market . $L T A _ { c }$ is the long-term ambition score of country or market . $G M M _ { c }$ is the government and market mechanisms score of country or market . The near-term ambition of a country is assessed by considering the annual emissions reduction rate needed to meet their publicly disclosed near-term climate targets. Countries with aggressive near-term targets have high emissions reduction rates and therefore a higher policy pressure segment score. A country or market’s long-term ambition indicates the strength and credibility of its long-term climate targets such as net-zero commitments. Long term targets could signal the direction of future policy and regulatory developments, even in the near term. The government and market mechanisms score indicates the current strength of policy and marketbased mechanisms signaling a government’s commitment to driving the energy transition. This score is calculated as the average of carbon pricing score and fossil fuel subsidies score. $$ G M M _ { c } = A v g \left( \mathit { C P M } , \mathit { F F S } \right) $$ Where Carbon Pricing Mechanisms score Fossil Fuel Subsidies score. Carbon pricing mechanisms score indicates mechanisms such as carbon taxes or emissions trading systems that exert policy pressure on companies by assigning a direct cost to carbon emissions. The fossil fuel subsidies score indicates the degree of financial support for fossil fuel consumption. Lower subsidies (higher scores) increase transition pressure by removing cost advantages, whereas high subsidies (lower scores) signal continued alignment with fossil fuel-based economic structures, thus reducing policy pressure In the absence of evidence from data sources indicating that a country has near- or long-term emissions reduction targets or carbon pricing mechanisms in place, a score of 0 is assigned. In the absence of a country’s fossil fuel subsidy information, a score of 5 is assigned. ## Data sources The following sources are used to determine the Opportunities in Green Building Exposure score: International Monetary Fund (IMF) Implied Mitigation Targets, Net Zero Tracker, Carbon Pricing Dashboard, IMF Fossil Fuel subsidies data; Department of Energy; ENERGY STAR Portfolio Manager, Environmental Protection Agency; Refinitiv; MSCI S&C; company disclosures. ## Contact us ## About MSCI Inc. MSCI (NYSE: MSCI Inc.) strengthens global markets by connecting participants across the financial ecosystem with a common language. Our research-based data, analytics and indexes, supported by advanced technology, set standards for global investors and help our clients understand risks and opportunities so they can make better decisions and unlock innovation. We serve asset managers and owners, privatemarket sponsors and investors, hedge funds, wealth managers, banks, insurers and corporates. To learn more, please visit www.msci.com msci.com/contact-us The process for submitting a formal index complaint can be found on the index regulation page of MSCI’s website at: https://www.msci.com/index-regulation. ## About MSCI Sustainability and Climate Products and Services MSCI Sustainability and Climate products and services are provided by MSCI Solutions LLC and certain related entities, and are designed to provide in-depth research, ratings and analysis of environmental, social and governance related business practices to companies worldwide. sections.title_en: Introduction

blocks.content: This document provides essential information on the components of the Opportunities in Renewable Energy Key Issue to enable users of ESG Ratings to understand how MSCI Sustainability & Climate’s (MSCI S&C’s)1 outputs are determined. Opportunities in Renewable Energy is a Key Issue in the Environmental Pillar of the MSCI ESG Ratings model. Companies are evaluated on their positioning to meet market demand for renewable power through capacity additions and network expansion.
For additional details on the MSCI ESG Ratings Model, refer to the Data, ratings and scores section of “ESG Ratings Methodology.”

sections.title_en: Opportunities in Renewable Energy Key Issue score

blocks.content: The Opportunities in Renewable Energy Key Issue score evaluates the company’s level of exposure to, and management of, opportunities on this Key Issue. The Key Issue score on this Key Issue is based on the Exposure score and the Management score using the formula below. The Exposure score and the Management score are combined such that the Exposure score determines the weight placed on the Management score, ranging from 50% (when the Exposure score is equal to zero) to 100% (when the Exposure score is equal to 10).

$$
K I _ { i } = \left( \left( \frac { E X P _ { i } } { 2 0 } + . 5 \right) \times M G M T _ { i } \right) + \left( \left( . 5 - \frac { E X P _ { i } } { 2 0 } \right) \times 5 \right)
$$
Where:
$K I _ { i }$ is the Key Issue score for company i.
$E X P _ { i }$ is the Exposure score for company i.
$M G M T _ { i }$ is the Management score for company i.

sections.title_en: Opportunities in Renewable Energy Strategy score

blocks.content: The Opportunities in Renewable Energy Strategy score evaluates the company’s initiatives to expand renewable energy capacity through strategic investments, internal structures, and quantitative targets. It is expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates strong initiatives.

sections.title_en: • Targets to increase renewable capacity

blocks.content: Definition: Indicates whether the company has disclosed quantitative targets to increase renewable energy capacity. Includes targets referring to owned capacity only, i.e., excluding purchasing agreements. Applies to companies with an electricity generation business only.

sections.title_en: • Internal structures to develop renewable capacity

blocks.content: Definition: Assesses the company’s established internal structures related to developing renewable capacity. Best practice is to have a dedicated renewable energy subsidiary or be wholly involved in renewables. Applies to companies with an electricity generation business only.

sections.title_en: • Investments to increase connection of renewable power to electric grid

blocks.content: Definition: Indicates whether the company has made investments related to the increased connection of renewable power to the electric grid. Applies to companies with an electricity transmission or distribution business only.

sections.title_en: • Score of planned additional renewable electricity generation relative to current total capacity

blocks.content: Definition: Assesses the company’s performance on ratio of planned additional renewable electricity generation to current total capacity. Expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates the highest level of performance.

sections.title_en: ◦ Current Total Installed Capacity (MW)

blocks.content: Definition: The current amount of installed capacity for power generation in megawatts (MW).

sections.title_en: ◦ Additional renewable capacity (MW)

blocks.content: Definition: The amount of capacity in megawatts (MW) that an issuer has disclosed as planned additions which are renewables.

sections.title_en: Opportunities in Renewable Energy Programs & Initiatives score

blocks.content: The Opportunities in Renewable Energy Programs & Initiatives score evaluates the company’s initiatives to expand renewable energy opportunities through customer green power options and commercialization of renewable power equipment. It is expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates strong initiatives.

sections.title_en: • Commercializes renewable power equipment

blocks.content: Definition: Indicates whether the company implements programs that involve the installation of equipment used in renewable energy generation.

sections.title_en: • Offers customers a green power option

blocks.content: Definition: Indicates whether the company offers its customers the option to purchase power from renewable generation sources. Applies to companies with an electricity supply business only.

sections.title_en: Opportunities in Renewable Energy Performance score

blocks.content: The Opportunities in Renewable Energy Performance score evaluates the company’s performance on opportunities in renewable energy metrics (including renewable capacity and percentage change in the proportion of renewable capacity to total generation capacity) relative to its peers. It is expressed as a 0- 10 score, where 10 indicates the highest level of performance.

sections.title_en: • Renewable power capacity performance relative to peers

blocks.content: Definition: Assesses the company's performance on total renewable energy power capacity (as a percentage of total installed capacity), and trend in renewable energy power capacity, relative to its peers. Expressed as a 0-10 score, where 10 indicates the highest level of performance.

sections.title_en: ◦ Renewable power capacity (% of total installed capacity) score

blocks.content: Definition: Assesses the company’s performance on installed renewable power capacity expressed (as a percentage of total installed capacity). Expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates strong performance.

The Business and Geographic Exposure scores are scored on a 0-10 scale, with 10 corresponding to the highest opportunity and 0 corresponding to the lowest opportunity. Refer to the Analyzing risk exposure section of “ESG Ratings Methodology” for additional details. The following formula is used in the Exposure score calculation:

$$
E X P _ { O R E , i } = B U S _ { O R E , i } ( 1 + 0 . 1 \big ( G E O _ { O R E , i } - 5 \big ) )
$$

MSCI ESG Ratings Methodology: Opportunities in Renewable Energy Key Issue ## Contents Introduction. 3 Opportunities associated with this Key Issue 4 Opportunities in Renewable Energy Key Issue score . 4 Opportunities in Renewable Energy Management Framework... . 5 Opportunities in Renewable Energy Management score ... . 5 Opportunities in Renewable Energy Strategy score .6 Opportunities in Renewable Energy Programs & Initiatives score... . 7 Opportunities in Renewable Energy Performance score . .8 Opportunities in Renewable Energy Exposure score... 8 Business Exposure score. . 9 Business Segment Exposure scores.. 10 Geographic Exposure score . . 10 Geographic Segment Exposure scores... . 11 Data sources.. . 12 Contact us. .13 ## Introduction This document provides essential information on the components of the Opportunities in Renewable Energy Key Issue to enable users of ESG Ratings to understand how MSCI Sustainability & Climate’s (MSCI S&C’s)1 outputs are determined. Opportunities in Renewable Energy is a Key Issue in the Environmental Pillar of the MSCI ESG Ratings model. Companies are evaluated on their positioning to meet market demand for renewable power through capacity additions and network expansion. For additional details on the MSCI ESG Ratings Model, refer to the Data, ratings and scores section of “ESG Ratings Methodology.” Exhibit 1: MSCI ESG Key Issue hierarchy

## Opportunities associated with this Key Issue • Increased revenues from utilizing public subsidies. • Increased revenue due to changing consumer demand. • Increased access to markets due to renewable power generation mandates (state, national or regional objectives). • Increased market share in specific market segments due to early-mover status. ## Opportunities in Renewable Energy Key Issue score The Opportunities in Renewable Energy Key Issue score evaluates the company’s level of exposure to, and management of, opportunities on this Key Issue. The Key Issue score on this Key Issue is based on the Exposure score and the Management score using the formula below. The Exposure score and the Management score are combined such that the Exposure score determines the weight placed on the Management score, ranging from 50% (when the Exposure score is equal to zero) to 100% (when the Exposure score is equal to 10). $$ K I _ { i } = \left( \left( \frac { E X P _ { i } } { 2 0 } + . 5 \right) \times M G M T _ { i } \right) + \left( \left( . 5 - \frac { E X P _ { i } } { 2 0 } \right) \times 5 \right) $$ Where: $K I _ { i }$ is the Key Issue score for company i. $E X P _ { i }$ is the Exposure score for company i. $M G M T _ { i }$ is the Management score for company i. ## Opportunities in Renewable Energy Management Framework The table below outlines the indicators mapped to their respective components that inform the Opportunities in Renewable Energy Management score. MSCI S&C assigned each indicator a default weight. Indicator weights may be adjusted at the company level to reflect the relevance of the indicator to the company’s business activities. If a company has no exposure to the business activities covered by an indicator, the indicator is assigned a weight of zero.
